blocks.text: A challenge needs identity, validity, intended device and a decision reference. The contract does not carry selfies or documents into the general UI; it transmits the minimum necessary state. Revocation must override an approval not yet consumed, and queries must reflect that without silently restarting the case.

Retention policy distinguishes biometric material, review decisions and operational logs. Each category needs appropriate access and duration. Evidence storage should not become a permanent archive for technical convenience. Ownership comes from a verified session, not a value chosen in a public request body, even though the lab accepts strings directly.

blocks.caption: Literal lab tests; count and result come from an actual run.

blocks.text: The 14 tests verify single use under concurrency, exact expiration, a different device, wrong holder, revocation, missing evidence and misleading truthy values. The most important test confirms that declaring a camera problem authorizes nothing. Another shows that an incorrect challenge does not make a later attempt succeed without review.

Real capture, liveness, accessibility and storage tests are still missing. Those belong to different layers with their own criteria. I would add network-interruption and device-change drills during recovery, checking that an approved decision remains bound to the correct context rather than moving to another device.

Legitimate completion and account takeover must be read together. Higher conversion that authorizes the wrong people is a regression even if support volume falls. Collection segments physical barriers, permissions and review without making raw biometrics an analytics dimension.

The pilot retains a comparable cohort of eligible journeys and observes repeat contacts for seven days, plus fraud signals over the identity team’s chosen window. Comprehension testing includes people with capture limitations. Any confirmed increase in unauthorized access stops expansion; longer review time also requires checking whether the flow merely moved work to specialists.

Assumptions are 3,000 / 8,000 / 15,000 monthly recoveries, 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6 contacts avoided per journey and BRL 9.00 per contact. The alternative may add review: assume 0.10 / 0.08 / 0.05 additional reviews per journey at BRL 18.00. Operations add BRL 3,000.00 / BRL 6,000.00 / BRL 10,000.00 monthly, with hypothetical implementation of BRL 110,000.00.

The formula deducts additional review before operations. Better routing is therefore not automatically cheaper. No customer balance enters the calculation because none was published. Residual fraud must be measured as a guardrail and budgeted if an attributable difference exists; no unsupported antifraud benefit is assumed. Support capacity becomes cash savings only when realizable spending falls.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 110,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL -36,000.00 / BRL 135,360.00 / BRL 690,000.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

The first milestone aligns identity, mobile and accessibility on alternatives already available. The second instruments barrier reasons without collecting sensitive material. The third builds resumability and tracking in a controlled environment. Only then does a pilot measure whether people reach the correct channel with fewer repeated attempts.

The EM must reserve human-review capacity before increasing intake. Staff defines binding and revocation contracts with device owners. More routing without review capacity can worsen waiting, so acceptance covers queue quality rather than screens alone. The proposed timeline may change after discovery.

Rollout does not begin by disabling facial recognition. It begins by making an approved alternative discoverable and trackable. Identity on-call receives alerts for repeated use, mismatched context and consumption failures; support is instructed not to request material through improvised channels.

Drills include a challenge expiring during review, holder revocation and approval followed by connection loss. Resumption queries existing state before opening another case. Rollback preserves decisions and retains previous assisted channels. If evidence-to-device binding is uncertain, the response is renewed authorized review rather than release for convenience.

As Staff, I would separate device capability from identity confidence so a UI simplification cannot contaminate authorization. I would reject a rule accepting any photograph after a camera error: a physical problem does not make evidence more trustworthy. A sound alternative requires policy, review and single-use binding.

As EM, I would coordinate mobile, identity, privacy and support around a journey the organization can operate. This includes specialist capacity and training as well as code. My proposed contribution makes security and accessibility joint quality criteria while remaining transparent about what the lab demonstrates and what requires further validation.

I would also avoid a conversion target that pressures reviewers to approve uncertain cases. The EM should track decision quality, workload and escalation while Staff keeps the protocol capable of representing waiting and additional review. Recovery may legitimately take longer when evidence is missing. The desired improvement removes unproductive repetition and improves guidance while preserving the security decision the case requires. That distinction helps a team discuss tradeoffs honestly and prevents a convenient completion metric from becoming the only definition of success.

Handoff requires an approved alternative-method policy, session service, restricted storage and retention plan. It also requires real-hardware testing, interruption support and fraud monitoring. Progress depends on better legitimate recovery without weakened identity. If review capacity dominates the problem, I prioritize the queue before adding more app steps.

chapters.title: New phone, missing verification code
chapters.subtitle: Recover contact without confusing email proof with authorization.
chapters.source_title: Reclame AQUI — public complaint and response

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.title: Answered · RA 242544191
blocks.text: On March 6, 2026, a customer reported changing phones, not knowing or accessing the previous email and receiving no code at a newly supplied address. On March 13, Nubank explained additional checks and said a device had been authorized on March 9. It was awaiting a reply to private guidance. The record is answered, with no public final confirmation from the customer. The cause of delivery failure is unproven.

An authorized device does not by itself prove that the person completed the entire reported journey. The response may indicate meaningful progress, but it does not turn answered into resolved. This case concerns email, not SMS or a broken camera. Private messages were not inspected. The proposal uses the reported barrier to examine the contract between updated contact, delivered code, validated code and a new-device session.

sources.title: Reclame AQUI — public complaint and response

blocks.text: The report supports investigation of delivery, generation binding and journey comprehension, but identifies no provider, bounce or spam filter. I would trace a recovery_id across change request, issuance, provider acceptance, delivery feedback and validation. SMTP acceptance means neither reading nor identity proof.

One hypothesis is that the customer cannot distinguish the active contact from the challenge that remains valid after resending. Logs and research can refute this: if contact and challenge are consistent, the bottleneck may lie elsewhere. I would not claim a root cause from a “did not arrive” message alone.

Delivery investigation must acknowledge incomplete feedback. Some providers report acceptance without delivery confirmation; others produce delayed or duplicated events. I would document which signals are observations and which are inferences, keeping customer messages consistent with that distinction. A newly supplied address still requires identity validation before changing account contact. Research should observe whether people understand that confirming contact and recovering access can require different steps. Otherwise, a technically accurate delivery message may create the false expectation that the account should already be available.

blocks.title: New phone, missing verification code
blocks.caption: Independent proposed architecture; suggested technologies, not Nubank internal infrastructure.

blocks.text: The versioned contact feeds issuance and verification. Policy sets limits while the record retains the current challenge. The verifier rechecks generation before consuming a code, preventing a concurrent change from leaving an old challenge usable.

The app receives contact progress separately from access. Confirming an address is only one step; device authorization remains in the identity domain. The diagram does not treat the delivery provider as an authority on account ownership.

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from the executed independent lab; remaining validation is in the complete file.

blocks.text: ContactRecovery.verify rejects obsolete generation, invalid time, missing challenge and exhausted attempt budget. A hash compares the code without retaining its plain text in the educational record. Success consumes the challenge and sets verified to true; device_authorized remains false.

The lab accepts fixed codes for reproducible tests. A real service must generate random secrets, limit distributed abuse and protect storage. A simple hash of a short code is insufficient against database extraction; appropriate secret and key design is required. The purpose is lifecycle and binding verification rather than a production-ready authentication service.

blocks.caption: Proposed integration example, not executed; this is not Nubank internal code.

blocks.text: The TypeScript contract uses an explicit union to distinguish pending contact, confirmed contact and authorized device. This helps UI review, but static types do not validate network input. The adapter must still validate schema, origin and scope before constructing the object.

Messages neither expose a complete email address nor reveal account existence to unauthenticated requesters. Resend displays a policy-consistent deadline and preserves the journey. I would reuse the existing delivery provider where possible, adding correlation and event handling instead of assuming that switching providers solves an unknown cause.

blocks.text: Generation changes only after an authorized contact update. Each issuance replaces the prior challenge within that generation and applies cooldown. TTL belongs to the challenge while attempt limits belong to abuse policy. Production needs additional account, device and source limits that survive restarts and multiple instances.

Delivery events should distinguish accepted, bounced and expired without concluding that a message was read. The public record provides none of these events. Logs exclude codes and full addresses; investigation uses protected references. Contact change must not allow an attacker to choose a destination freely and become the holder by receiving their own code.

def test_contact_change_invalidates_old_code(self):
        self.r.change_contact("a", "other@example.test", True)
        self.r.issue("a", "654321", 110, 60)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.r.verify("a", 1, "123456", 120)
        self.assertTrue(self.r.verify("a", 2, "654321", 120))

    def test_contact_proof_does_not_authorize_device(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.r.verify("a", 1, "123456", 120))
        self.assertTrue(self.r.verified)
        self.assertFalse(self.r.device_authorized)
blocks.caption: Literal lab tests; count and result come from an actual run.

blocks.text: The 14 tests cover contact change with an old code, resend, attempt limits, expiration, future clock, replay and wrong holder. The state-separation test confirms that email validation does not authorize a device. This invariant prevents a delivery mechanism from becoming complete identity proof.

The suite sends no email and measures no deliverability. Provider events, cross-process limits and timing-based enumeration tests remain missing. Before production, I would add coordinated resend attacks and two sessions changing contact concurrently, plus integration with the real identity-recovery policy.

The funnel must show issuance, observable delivery, contact validation and authorization without treating them as equivalent. I would measure repeat contacts per recovery and time per stage, segmented by provider and app version where volume is sufficient to preserve privacy.

The experiment compares eligible journeys of similar complexity and observes legitimate recovery, messages sent and review load. Better delivery accompanied by more abuse does not pass acceptance. Expansion stops for accepted obsolete codes, account-data leakage or account takeover attributable to the flow. Baselines remain unknown until instrumentation and identity-team validation.

Assumptions are 10,000 / 30,000 / 60,000 monthly journeys, repeat-contact reductions of 0.05 / 0.12 / 0.18 and BRL 8.00 marginal cost per contact. Additional messages are 15,000 / 45,000 / 90,000 at BRL 0.03 each, plus BRL 4,000.00 / BRL 7,000.00 / BRL 12,000.00 monthly operations. Hypothetical implementation costs BRL 100,000.00.

Net benefit is journeys × avoided repeat contacts × cost, less messages and operations. Global average revenue per customer is not used to value recovered access; that would require causal incremental revenue and margin evidence unavailable in this complaint. The conservative scenario may be negative, showing that sending more messages without sufficiently reducing confusion does not justify investment through avoided cost.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 100,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL -5,400.00 / BRL 245,400.00 / BRL 860,400.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

The roadmap starts with an inventory of available events and contact-recovery methods. Identity validates which changes require review; the delivery owner explains what callbacks actually mean. Product defines progress messages that do not reveal account data.

Shadow mode compares issued and consumed generations before changing resend or experience. The EM coordinates provider dependencies and review capacity; Staff resolves concurrency and policy persistence. If observability reveals a predominantly external problem, the plan should prioritize the adapter and communication instead of unnecessarily rebuilding authentication.

During canary rollout, old and new issuers must share generation control. A UI flag cannot stop an incompatible backend from accepting an old code. Migration requires compatibility or explicit exclusion of versions that do not understand the new identity.

The drill includes late delivery feedback, concurrent resend and contact change while a code is in transit. Operations must distinguish provider delay from an already-revoked challenge. Rollback preserves generations and limits rather than reactivating old secrets. Abuse alerts go to identity; aggregate delivery failures go to the channel owner.

As Staff, I would propose generation binding and the separation between contact possession and device authorization. I would reject accepting any unexpired code: two contacts and two resends can leave several contradictory proofs apparently valid. The challenge must be current in the correct context.

As EM, I would organize delivery across security, messaging and mobile, including abuse tests in the definition of done. I would also ensure support sees the same progress without accessing secrets. These are proposed technical and coordination actions, not claims of authority or prior results inside Nubank.

The technical decision must withstand pressure to remove steps without understanding their purpose. I would explain which controls are necessary for risk and which repetitions result only from poorly preserved state. As EM, I would organize a support review using anonymized journeys so the people receiving customer questions participate in design. This produces a more operable solution and avoids adding another resend button without fixing context. blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.title: Answered · RA 240394695
blocks.text: On February 10, 2026, a customer reported disputing an unrecognized Airbnb purchase and being unable to add evidence while it was under review. On February 18, Nubank reported provisional credit, a dispute opened on February 11, cancellation of the virtual card and disabling the automatic updater. Amounts are masked. There is no public final outcome or confirmation that the attachment channel was reopened.

The concrete barrier is adding material after opening the case, not proving here whether the purchase was fraudulent. The confirmation attributed to Airbnb is in private material that was not examined. Provisional credit must remain distinct from the dispute outcome. The proposal does not promise that a card network will accept every late document; it aims to preserve material, explain its stage and provide a traceable admissibility decision.

sources.title: Reclame AQUI — public complaint and response

blocks.text: An “under review” state may be blocking every edit even though adding evidence and changing the original claim carry different risks. This is a hypothesis, not a proven app cause. I would map internal stages and external deadlines to identify where additional evidence can still be considered.

Investigation compares upload attempts, contacts requesting submission and analyst decisions. It must distinguish UI restrictions, format limits, quarantine and network cutoffs. If material was already outside the applicable deadline, improvement may mean an explanation and an allowed route rather than implying engineering can unilaterally reopen the dispute.

I would also distinguish supplementary evidence from correcting the disputed transaction itself. The former may be appended without changing case identity; the latter may require reviewing the object of the dispute. If both use one generic edit button, it becomes difficult to explain what was actually received. The proposed design records submission intent and traceability so an analyst can determine its relationship to earlier material. This avoids treating every later document as either a harmless addition or an unauthorized change when its meaning requires judgment.

blocks.text: Upload enters quarantine and retains identity before reaching the dossier. Holder scope protects both intake and submission. Dossier policy determines what can proceed after review without deleting earlier evidence.

The app response distinguishes received, being checked, available for analysis and submitted. Receiving bytes does not confirm merit or external acceptance. The design also keeps this state separate from provisional credit or a final financial decision.

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from the executed independent lab; remaining validation is in the complete file.

blocks.text: Dossier.append checks scope, size and upload identity before creating a version. Repeating the same key and content returns the previous record; reusing the key with different bytes creates a conflict. A copy is returned so callers cannot accidentally mutate internal state.

Material received after cutoff is retained as late, but submit does not promise submission in that window. The scanner is a simulated boundary: a trusted boolean represents an already-verified external verdict. The lab neither scans malware nor stores cloud files. Its contract preserves versions and separates receipt from eligibility.

blocks.caption: Proposed integration example, not executed; this is not Nubank internal code.

blocks.text: The storage example defines references and states rather than complete permissions. In an S 3 integration, I would design restricted upload, quarantine, content assessment and release to authorized analysts. Original objects and derivatives need distinct identities so metadata removal does not destroy the original evidentiary reference.

The dispute service decides admissibility and deadline; storage does not assume that authority. Temporary URLs must not become public history links. The UI can show a safe name, size and receipt without rendering active content. This TypeScript example is illustrative and was neither executed nor connected to AWS services.

The model does not allow silent attachment replacement. Corrections become new versions with an explicit relationship to the previous one. def test_late_evidence_is_retained_without_submission_promise(self):
        item = self.upload(now=101)
        self.d.scan(item["version"], True, True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.d.submit(item["version"], "dispute-analyst", True)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.d.items), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.d.items[0]["state"], "reviewable")

    def test_reused_upload_id_cannot_replace_evidence(self):
        original = self.upload()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.upload(data=b"replacement")
        self.assertEqual(self.d.items[0]["digest"], original["digest"])
blocks.caption: Literal lab tests; count and result come from an actual run.

blocks.text: The 14 tests verify retained late material without a submission promise, identity conflict, quarantine, rejected content, scope, replay and mutation of returned data. The exact cutoff is considered late in this model and must be checked against the real rule before integration.

The replacement test protects earlier evidence while the quarantine test prevents completed upload from appearing immediately usable. The suite does not validate real file types, antivirus, accessibility or network rules. I would add malformed-file and interrupted-upload tests, plus restoring the relationship after a temporary URL expires.

Success is not simply more attachments. The main metric tracks eligible material received with a receipt and reviewed within a useful window. More irrelevant documents can increase cost and delay decisions, so analyst time and admissibility must also be observed.

The pilot compares disputes at similar stages and with similar reasons, reviewed by analysts familiar with deadlines. Repeat contacts are measured per dossier over seven days. No chargeback result is attributed to the improvement without an appropriate comparison because merit and merchant behavior affect outcomes. Document exposure, evidence substitution or a missed deadline immediately stops expansion.

The financial model uses analyst rework without inventing the masked purchase amount. Assumptions are 2,000 / 6,000 / 12,000 monthly dossiers, 4 / 6 / 8 minutes saved per dossier, BRL 75.00 per hour and realizable shares of 25% / 40% / 50%. Additional uploads are 3,000 / 9,000 / 18,000 at BRL 0.20 each, plus BRL 3,000.00 / BRL 6,000.00 / BRL 10,000.00 monthly operations. Hypothetical implementation costs BRL 140,000.00.

The calculation deducts file checks and operations from monetizable capacity. If capacity does not lower spending, I report hours rather than cash. Principal potentially recovered to the customer stays outside this formula. Improved dispute outcomes enter a separate analysis only after causality and the actual beneficiary are established.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 140,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL -13,200.00 / BRL 122,400.00 / BRL 556,800.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

Dispute operations leads the stage and cutoff map; security defines the upload boundary; privacy reviews custody and retention. Staff connects these contracts so an apparently small app change does not create an ungoverned document channel.

The first prototype receives synthetic attachments, generates a receipt and shows analysts only released material. A limited cohort then validates usefulness and cost. The EM secures training and capacity for greater intake. If an external cutoff prevents consideration, delivery is limited to a permitted route and explanation without promising that every piece of evidence changes the result.

Rollout enables receipt before automating any external submission. Analysts remain accountable for admissibility; a flag cannot make every attachment accepted evidence. Security on-call watches quarantine failures while dispute operations tracks material near cutoff.

The drill injects duplicate upload, an unavailable scanner and a delayed callback. The safe state keeps the file restricted and explains pending work. Rollback closes new intake through the new flow while preserving receipts and authorized access to received material. Preserving evidence is as important as avoiding improper submission.

As Staff, I would propose immutable additional evidence rather than freely reopening the entire form. This preserves the original claim and makes changes auditable. The rejected alternative is overwriting the earlier attachment: it simplifies the screen but loses context and may confuse review.

As EM, I would coordinate dispute operations, mobile, security and privacy, placing analyst capacity and training in the same plan as development. The proposed contribution turns a concrete barrier into an operable flow without promising chargeback success or attributing financial results to a code example.

A hiring discussion can explore how I would negotiate minimum scope with operations: the first gain may be a receipt and routing before automated submission. As Staff, I would document that boundary to reduce risk; as EM, I would ensure the team is not held accountable for a network outcome it does not control. The commitment would cover intact receipt, review within the applicable window and correct information, measured separately from financial victory. This helps prioritize a useful first delivery without disguising external dependencies as implementation details.

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.title: Answered · RA 228360515
blocks.text: On October 2, 2025, a customer reported three Pix transfers totaling BRL 478.55 for CCXP 25 tickets and said she notified Nubank within two hours of recognizing a scam. She requested MED updates. Nubank reported starting the process and described seven calendar days plus four for conditional reimbursement. No individual outcome or recovered amount was published. This is a historical 2025 response, not a complete description of current rules.

The public response associates absent email with an unaccepted claim or unavailable funds but does not identify which outcome occurred in this case. A customer needs an explicit outcome when evidence exists and ongoing tracking when it does not. Police reports, receipts and private chat were not inspected. The quoted amount is alleged customer exposure, not independently verified final loss or potential bank revenue.

pages.chapter_title: MED: track progress without promising a refund

pages.title: Diagnosis before design

blocks.text: Diagnosis separates interbank progress from message delivery to the customer. Missing email does not reveal whether a case is under analysis, rejected, unfunded or affected by a communication failure. The engineering hypothesis is that explicit states and a next update reduce uncertainty-driven contacts.

I would reconstruct received events, available projection and emitted notifications per case without inferring that delay caused the receiving account to be emptied. The source does not demonstrate that causality. The episode occurred in 2025; a current implementation must map 2026 contracts and rules with Pix, risk and legal rather than judging historical conduct against later requirements.

The timeline should explain partial recovery without turning the remainder into a debt owed by the bank. It must also distinguish operational closure from definitive impossibility of any future recovery under the applicable contract. I would not fill event gaps with a probable outcome merely to simplify the screen. When information is unconfirmed, the next action is investigation and communication of the limitation, preserving the ability to update state when authorized evidence arrives. This makes uncertainty visible without inventing either a positive or negative financial promise.

blocks.text: The adapter verifies origin before persistence. The normalizer translates the effective version into an internal contract; the validator protects transitions and amounts before publishing the timeline. App and support share that authorized view.

Reconciliation compares expected history with the state explained to the customer. The lab’s sequence is internal to its adapter and does not claim to reproduce official DICT fields. A gap blocks progress and requires recovery rather than inventing an outcome.

blocks.text: RecoveryTimeline.apply preserves each event’s identity and payload. It accepts only the next sequence; delayed events or gaps require reconciliation and controlled retry. A partial return must be positive and cannot exceed the remaining claimed amount. Closing a case adds no money.

The function checks authority before recognizing replay and rejects booleans as monetary values. The model neither blocks accounts nor calls participants and does not implement every regulatory state. It demonstrates a communication projection that conserves cents. Reopening or new rules require an explicit additional contract rather than an improvised transition.

The real adapter requires authentication and mapping to the effective official contract, reviewed with the Pix domain. Synthetic names are not presented as production fields. def test_partial_refund_replay_never_doubles_money(self):
        self.event("analysis", 1, "analyzing")
        self.event("refund-a", 2, "partial", 20000)

The lab also prevents silence from closing a case. It does not test actual recipient funds, scheme communication or regulatory deadlines. blocks.text: The main indicator measures delay between a confirmed event and queryable state, segmented by stage and contract version. I also track cases without a next update, uncertainty-driven contacts and displayed-versus-confirmed amount discrepancies. These signals differ from the financial recovery rate.

Evaluation uses comparable case cohorts, accounting for reporting time, profile and recoverability. A clearer timeline may reduce contacts without recovering one additional cent; that can still be useful but must be described accurately. It also supports a more honest investment decision: better clarity may justify its operating cost without being presented as proof that the underlying recovery mechanism became more effective.

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: On 14 January 2026, complaint 237674561 described an unrecognized loan discovered after three overdue installments. Nubank replied that the loan had been contracted in March 2024 using an authorized device and password, with no irregularity identified. It maintained its refusal. The customer closed the case on 31 January as Not resolved. These are public accounts from parties in disagreement; they do not establish fraud or consent.

blocks.title: What this evidence supports
blocks.text: An opportunity to make investigation understandable and reviewable. The loan amount, individual agreement and complete signals are not public. The capture documents the complaint and response; it is not a forensic finding.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: Observed access does not settle consent

blocks.text: The engineering question starts at the boundary between evidence and conclusion. A record of an authorized device may matter to an investigation, but it should not be stored as a synonym for the account holder’s intent. This proposal separates access facts, the policy version applied, the reviewer’s interpretation and the communicated decision. A customer can then challenge a specific premise without restarting the entire conversation.

The falsifiable hypothesis is that some rework comes from incomplete dossiers or decisions whose reviewable reasoning is unclear. I would compare an authorized sample of cases with repeat contacts against what the agent could see at that time. If dossiers were already complete and understandable, the hypothesis weakens; the intervention may belong in policy, communication or another stage.

The study does not propose publishing fraud-control secrets or refunding every disputed loan. Financial decisions remain subject to approved authority and policy. The objective is consistent analysis with an owner, minimized evidence and a defined appeal. Legal and operational complexity requires specialist validation before setting deadlines or interim measures.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: A dossier with independent review

blocks.title: Separate facts, decisions and appeals
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The API authenticates the account holder and scopes access to the case. The durable record preserves actions before acknowledgment; triage organizes gaps without deciding fraud. The dossier supplies different customer and support projections with a shared revision reference.

Human review records the decision and policy in history. An appeal adds a stage rather than erasing the first decision. The exception path requires an independent reviewer in the model. Real identity, authorization and evidence retention are necessary integrations outside the laboratory.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: Core: revision and action identity

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_08.py; exercised by local tests.

blocks.text: The transaction checks expected revision, action identity and authorized role. An identical retry returns history without duplicating the event; reusing the key with different content is a conflict. This contract prevents two concurrent decisions from advancing the same revision.

The laboratory represents one case and receives roles from trusted context. It neither authenticates people nor determines whether the loan is legitimate. validate_transition requires evidence before a decision and protects appeal independence. The local database demonstrates persistence; it does not represent the institution’s actual storage.

pages.title: Make the policy explicit

blocks.code:
(defn reviewable? [{:keys [evidence decision policy]}]
  (and (seq evidence)
       (string? policy)
       (every? #(contains? % :source-ref) evidence)
       (not= :device-access-only decision)))

(defn appeal-command [case-id revision reviewer]
  {:case-id case-id
   :expected-revision revision
   :action :independent-review
   :reviewer reviewer})
blocks.caption: Illustrative Clojure example, not executed; integration and policy require validation.

blocks.text: A pure function can check structural completeness before routing the dossier. It cannot turn the presence of data into a correct verdict. The example rejects a simplified decision category based only on device access; this is a proposed rule for the study, not a known Nubank rule.

In the service, the reviewer identifier must come from authenticated identity rather than the customer’s request body. Policy has an immutable version, effective period and owner. Policy changes need approved examples and operational review, because a technically correct deployment can still produce inappropriate decisions. Kafka would carry minimized references; sensitive attachments would remain in restricted storage.

pages.title: Evidence and access contracts

blocks.caption: Synthetic illustrative contract; not a payload captured from the app.

blocks.text: A hash helps identify evidence but does not prove its truth or replace chain of custody. Retention policy determines how long the object can be consulted; the projection should not retain unnecessary copies. Administrative access needs a recorded purpose and must be auditable by an independent team.

pages.title: Test appeal and recovery

blocks.code:
def test_appeal_requires_independent_reviewer(self):
        self.seed()
        self.d.append('a', 2, 'owner', 'customer', 'appeal', {})
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionError):
            self.d.append('r', 3, 'r1', 'reviewer', 'review', {'policy': 'v2'})
        self.assertEqual(len(self.d.history()), 3)
        self.d.append('r', 3, 'r2', 'reviewer', 'review', {'policy': 'v2'})
        self.assertEqual(self.d.history()[1]['evidence']['policy'], 'v1')

    def test_restart_and_retry_preserve_one_evidence(self):
        self.d.append('e', 0, 'a', 'analyst', 'evidence', self.ev)
        self.d.close()
        self.d = Dispute(self.path)
        result = self.d.append('e', 0, 'a', 'analyst', 'evidence', self.ev)
        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
        self.assertNotIn('consent', result[0]['evidence'])
blocks.caption: Literal excerpts; the complete local suite passed 9 tests.

blocks.text: The first assertion protects appeal independence and verifies that rejection does not change history. The second closes and reopens the database, retries an action and confirms a single record. Other tests attack stale revisions, incorrect roles, missing evidence and sensitive payloads.

Tests do not assess human quality, evidence authenticity or policy fairness. Production work would add blinded sample review, cross-account access tests, permission expiry, export auditing and tool-outage exercises. A system that perfectly preserves a poor decision still needs process correction.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: Measure useful review and human effort

blocks.text: The baseline is unknown. I would instrument transitions with pseudonymized case_id, revision and timestamp; work time requires operational sampling rather than queue duration alone. Case age and actual effort are different measures. Unauthorized access and audit failures are additional guardrails.

The pilot would compare equivalent teams or periods using predefined eligibility, avoiding selection of easy cases only. Independent reviewers would assess samples from both groups. Expansion would stop for data exposure, lost evidence or a material deterioration in decision consistency, even if average handling time improved.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: Value: recovered capacity, not profit

blocks.text: Every input is assumed: 12,000, 24,000 or 40,000 annual dossiers; 8, 14 or 18 rework minutes saved; R$ 90 fully loaded hourly cost. Valued capacity is N × minutes ÷ 60 × 90. Implementation is assumed at R$ 240,000 and annual operations at R$ 60,000, 90,000 or 120,000. The final column subtracts both in year 1 and does not represent realized cash.

In the base case, 24,000 × 14 ÷ 60 × 90 = R$ 504,000; subtracting R$ 90,000 and R$ 240,000 leaves R$ 174,000 in modeled net capacity. Year-one break-even requires approximately 15,715 equivalent dossiers. Redistributing hours does not automatically save cash. Investment depends on confirming avoidable rework and identifying a concrete use for the released capacity.

blocks.title: Keep financial categories separate
blocks.text: Disputed principal and possible fraud are excluded. Loss estimates require verified exposure, confirmation and recovery. Do not aggregate benefits with other chapters that cover the same contacts.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: A 90-day plan with accountable roles

blocks.text: The calendar is a planning assumption. The critical dependency is authorized access to a sufficient sample, not building a screen. If evidence sources are incompatible, the first deliverable becomes identifying those gaps and assigning owners to resolve them.

The Engineering Manager coordinates capacity across lending, fraud, support and privacy; the Staff Engineer defines contracts and technical criteria. Policy review remains with its owners. Every phase ends with observable evidence and a recorded decision to continue, narrow or stop. The schedule does not promise changes dependent on external validation.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: Operate without abandoning the queue

blocks.text: Deployment starts in shadow mode: the new tool prepares dossiers while the existing operation continues making decisions. Completeness, preparation time and discrepancies are compared without automatically changing collections or credit. The next canary exposes tracking and review to a limited cohort, with human capacity reserved for appeals.

Alerts distinguish aging queues, unavailable evidence and authorization failure. Operations owns queue response; security owns exposure; the service team owns lost or duplicated events. A projection outage neither closes the case nor deletes its trail. Customers receive an honest stage and next action.

Rollback disables the new projection and automatic routing while preserving history and active cases. An exercise should simulate database failure after a decision, permission revocation during access and return of an old revision. The runbook must explain pending-work reconciliation and continuity communication without exporting dossiers to unprotected spreadsheets.

pages.chapter_title: Disputed loan: a decision must remain reviewable

pages.title: My contribution to the decision

blocks.text: As Staff, I would define the evidence model, authorization boundaries and review invariants. I would lead the consistency, retention and signal-exposure discussion using concrete disagreements. The most important decision would be to keep access records separate from interpretation of consent, preventing a technical field from carrying a conclusion it cannot support.

As Engineering Manager, I would establish joint delivery with operations and risk, an end-to-end owner and reserved review time. I would first prioritize the most frequent demonstrated rework, with explicit criteria for choosing product changes, integration or training as the next investment. These are proposed actions, not claims that I have managed Nubank teams or policies.

I would reject automatic refusal merely because the dossier contains a known device. I would also avoid exposing every signal to support. The proposal balances useful review with minimized access and accepts higher operational effort when needed to protect the quality of a sensitive decision.

blocks.text: The laboratory supports a joint review: engineering explains the contract; operations checks whether history reconstructs the work; risk evaluates decisions needing supervision; privacy evaluates exposure. Local execution validates only the modeled invariants, not the merits of a dispute.

The final gate is straightforward: proceed only if the sample shows a correctable gap, independent review maintains quality and released capacity has a destination. Otherwise retain the learning and choose another intervention. The intended result is a better-grounded decision that is easier to review, without promising automatic resolution of financial disputes.

chapters.subtitle: Receipt, allocation and projection need a shared contract
chapters.source_title: Reclame AQUI — statement payment and available credit

pages.title: 09 · Paid does not explain allocation

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: Complaint 242838873, dated 10 March 2026, describes a statement marked paid while credit was not fully restored, after three support tickets. On 17 March, Nubank reported correcting the statement, recognizing the payment and settling advanced installments. It explained credit restoration through processing and financed balances. The public status is Responded; no final customer confirmation is visible. Individual amounts are masked.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The response reports a correction but does not expose the ledger, event order or technical cause. This study proposes allocation traceability rather than diagnosing the responsible system.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: Three states, different consequences

blocks.text: Receiving money, applying money and refreshing a credit-limit view are separate stages. An interface can correctly report a payment while leaving unanswered which obligations were settled. With financing, the effect on available credit depends on rules that a single label cannot explain. The receipt must connect receipt of funds, destination and consequence rather than merely replace a word on screen.

My hypothesis is that some repeat contact comes from the absence of this verifiable link across channels. Investigation would use the payment identifier to reconstruct confirmation, allocations, compensating entries and projection updates. I would compare what the customer saw against support and ledger records at the same revision. If obligation calculation is wrong, improved presentation is insufficient and financial correction takes priority.

The responsibility boundary includes contractual financing rules and settlement recognition. The app cannot independently choose where to move money. It should also avoid inviting a second payment while the first allocation is uncertain. The proposal makes the pending state explicit and provides tracking under the same identifier.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: A receipt linked to the ledger

blocks.title: Verifiable allocation and versioned reading
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The allocator receives financial confirmation and applies a validated plan. The canonical receipt and its projection share a revision. The reconciler compares receipt values against independent invariants; a discrepancy is not solved by hiding cents in presentation.

Available-credit updates may run at a different pace, but must expose their revision and state. The diagram summarizes responsibilities, not every integration. Financial correction requires authorized compensating entries in the ledger; the reconciler detects and routes discrepancies without independently editing balances.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: Core: allocate or change nothing

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_09.py; SQLite represents one local authority.

blocks.text: The conditional write prevents applying more than an obligation owes. Allocations and receipt share a transaction: if the second destination is invalid, the first returns to its prior state as well. Unapplied funds remain explicit.

The example receives a preselected plan and does not implement Nubank’s contractual priority. Production selection requires versioned policy, account authorization and settlement evidence. A retry is accepted only when amount and plan are identical. Reusing the key to change destination requires a different authorized action, never a silent update.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: Pure rules, transactional writes

blocks.code:
(defn allocation-valid? [{:keys [received allocations unapplied]}]
  (and (pos-int? received)
       (every? pos-int? (vals allocations))
       (<= 0 unapplied)
       (= received (+ unapplied (reduce + (vals allocations))))))

(defn allocation-event [payment-id revision plan]
  {:event-type :payment-applied
   :payment-id payment-id
   :revision revision
   :allocations plan})
blocks.caption: Illustrative Clojure example, not executed; the Python laboratory is the tested artifact.

blocks.text: The function checks conservation but cannot prove that each obligation is eligible. That validation belongs inside the transactional boundary that knows balance, account holder and contract. Separating pure calculation from persistence helps test rules and review changes without attributing database guarantees to the function.

Event integration should persist allocation and publication intent atomically. The projection consumer deduplicates by identifier and financial revision. Transport ordering alone is insufficient: replay, reprocessing and consumer changes can redeliver the same fact. Publication failure leaves identifiable pending work, not permission to apply the payment again.

Identifiers must not expose accounts or contracts in public URLs. Support receives what is needed to explain allocation; third-party details and unrelated obligations remain protected. Rectification should reference the earlier fact and preserve the trail.

pages.title: Partial failure must not partially settle

blocks.code:
def test_failure_after_first_write_rolls_everything_back(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.l.apply('p', 20000, {'bill': 10000, 'installment': 6000})
        self.assertEqual(self.l.due('bill'), 10000)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.due('installment'), 5000)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.db.execute(
            'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM allocations').fetchone()[0], 0)

    def test_restart_retry_does_not_apply_twice(self):
        first = self.l.apply('p', 12000, {'bill': 10000})
        self.l.close()
        self.l = Ledger(self.path)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.apply('p', 12000, {'bill': 10000}), first)
        self.assertEqual(first['unapplied'], 2000)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.due('bill'), 0)
blocks.caption: Literal suite excerpts; 9 tests passed.

blocks.text: The partial-failure test attempts to settle one obligation and exceed another, verifying full rollback. The recovery test reopens the database and confirms that the same receipt cannot apply money twice. The suite also checks a residual cent, conflicting plan, fractional amount and payment against an already settled obligation.

Interest, fees, currency, reversals and cross-account authorization remain outside scope. An integration test should observe outbox and projection after failure between commit and publication, checking the receipt against an independent source. Local conservation is necessary but does not replace settlement-system reconciliation.

pages.title: Metrics that follow the payment

blocks.text: Baselines and internal deadlines are unknown. I would first define each timestamp’s origin: external confirmation, allocation commit and projection publication. Network delay must not be confused with settlement delay. Contact classification needs sampled review to distinguish a presentation question from a real financial error.

The experiment releases an explainable receipt without changing allocation rules. It compares equivalent cohorts by product, financing and amount. Expansion stops for any conservation violation, increased repeated payments or cross-account context leakage. Reducing contact must never incentivize hiding access to help.

pages.title: A financial case with two cost components

blocks.text: Every input is hypothetical: 60,000, 120,000 or 240,000 eligible payments/year; 0.06, 0.10 or 0.14 fewer contacts per payment; R$ 18 per contact. I additionally assume 1, 2 or 3 reconciliation hours saved per thousand payments at R$ 100/hour. Implementation: R$ 260,000; annual operations: R$ 60,000. Contacts and reconciliation hours must represent different work.

The base case is 120,000 × 0.10 × 18 + 120 × 2 × 100 = R$ 240,000 in annual capacity. Year one is R$ 240,000 − 60,000 − 260,000 = −R$ 80,000. Break-even requires 160,000 payments equivalent to the base assumption. This supports a pilot or reuse of components rather than automatic approval of the full project.

blocks.title: Do not convert balances into revenue
blocks.text: Restored credit and received principal are not profit. Capacity becomes cash only through concrete spending reductions. Exclude anticipation rework already measured in case 14.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: A reconciliation-led roadmap

blocks.text: The main dependency is a trustworthy financial reference against which to compare the new view. Without it, a dashboard can merely make an error more persuasive. In the first phase, accounting and credit approve examples for partial payments, financing, anticipation and compensation, with amounts in cents and explicit revisions.

The 90-day calendar is a planning scenario. The EM reserves support and operations capacity during the canary; the Staff Engineer defines failure tests and the correction contract. If reference quality fails the gate, the next delivery is reconciliation and remediation rather than visual expansion. Every exception needs an owner and a destination for unapplied funds.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: Rollback preserves financial writes

blocks.text: Launch starts with shadow reading. The projection calculates a receipt and compares it with the ledger without guiding customers or changing allocations. A canary then exposes the allocation explanation to eligible accounts. The old view remains an identified fallback, without mixing total and detail revisions.

Alerts combine unapplied-fund age, projection delay and sum violations. Platform owns publication; credit and statements own financial interpretation; operations coordinates customer resolution. An error queue should carry IDs and reasons rather than unnecessary complete financial data in broadly accessible logs.

Disabling the new receipt does not undo confirmed payments. Rollback affects presentation and routing, followed by reconciliation of pending work. Exercises include crashes before and after commit, a delayed consumer and concurrent correction. Throughout recovery, the tool must distinguish received from applied money for customers and support alike.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: My contribution on two fronts

blocks.text: As Staff, I would center the design on conservation and identity. I would choose the transaction boundary, define compensation and document which reads may be eventually consistent. I would reject inferring available credit from a paid-statement label because it replaces a financial contract with a visual approximation.

As Engineering Manager, I would bring together teams that may see different parts of the same payment. I would establish an end-to-end resolution owner and an investigation agreement using shared IDs. The plan must include support training and exception-handling capacity, not only a mobile component.

I would also advocate an economic decision proportional to the evidence. The base scenario does not recover implementation cost in the assumed first year. If an existing receipt API can be extended, the cost changes and must be recalculated. My role is to expose that tradeoff and protect journey integrity without presenting potential capacity as realized savings.

Proceeding requires a reconciled sample, demonstrated customer understanding and operations able to resolve differences. chapters.subtitle: An unknown outcome is a financial state, not an invitation to charge again
chapters.source_title: Reclame AQUI — NuPay duplication and interest

pages.title: 10 · Duplication with confirmed resolution

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: In complaint 241843991, dated 27 February 2026, the customer described an error message and repeated NuPay payment, followed by two R$ 900 transactions and R$ 81.17 interest. On 4 March, Nubank reported crediting the duplicate and interest; the customer confirmed resolution. The technical cause is not established.

rows: Do not invent a rounding adjustment

blocks.title: Resolved historical case
blocks.text: The one-cent discrepancy belongs to the account. The exact adjustment entry was not published; the response confirms categories rather than a numeric total.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: Timeout is not definitive failure

blocks.text: An interruption can occur after a partner accepts payment but before the app receives confirmation. During that interval, saying that nothing happened can induce another financial intent. This chapter hypothesizes that an explicit unknown-outcome state, paired with lookup of the original attempt, reduces unintended repetition without preventing legitimate new purchases.

Investigation must reconstruct identifiers, timestamps and contracts across client, service and provider. Retrying one intent must be distinguished from a deliberate second purchase. Amount, merchant and temporal proximity support analysis but are insufficient identity: two equal purchases may be legitimate. The public source cannot establish which mechanism was present or absent in the incident.

Control should begin before dispatch: create and persist intent, bind content to a key and recover state after app restart. If the provider lacks idempotency or reliable lookup, the guarantee weakens. The experience must then acknowledge uncertainty and initiate reconciliation rather than promise exactly one distributed execution.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: One intent crosses uncertainty

blocks.title: Resume the same payment
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The record binds key, amount, currency and recipient before dispatch. The provider retains the same key across attempts. Confirmation and reconciliation update the original intent, allowing the app to recover the receipt after losing the response.

The model uses two databases to represent the service/provider boundary. No distributed transaction spans them. The property explicitly depends on provider deduplication; without that capability, the design requires a different operational strategy and cannot retain the same promise.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: Core: persist before dispatch

blocks.code:
def pay(self, key, amount, merchant, timeout_after_provider=False):
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
            raise ValueError('nonempty intent identity required')
        if type(amount) is not int or amount <= 0 or not merchant:
            raise ValueError('invalid intent')
        payload = json.dumps([amount, merchant])
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            old = self.db.execute('SELECT payload,receipt FROM intents WHERE key=?',
                                  (key,)).fetchone()
            if old and old[0] != payload:
                raise ValueError('intent conflict')
            if old and old[1]:
                return old[1]
            self.db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO intents VALUES(?,?,NULL)',
                            (key, payload))
        receipt = self.provider.charge(key, payload)
        if timeout_after_provider:
            raise TimeoutError('provider committed; local outcome unknown')
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute('UPDATE intents SET receipt=? WHERE key=?',
                            (receipt, key))
        return receipt

    def state(self, key):
        row = self.db.execute('SELECT receipt FROM intents WHERE key=?',
                              (key,)).fetchone()
        return 'absent' if row is None else ('confirmed' if row[0] else 'unknown')
blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_10.py; two local databases and a synthetic provider.

blocks.text: Intent is recorded before the external call. The injected timeout occurs after provider commit but before the local receipt is saved. Recovery uses the same key and receives the existing receipt, demonstrating that missing a response does not authorize another effect.

A local transaction should not remain open while waiting on the network: this creates locks without making the partner an atomic participant. The laboratory exposes that separation. In production, payload includes account scope and contract; integration must address key retention, expiry and provider compatibility.

Local persistence helps app recovery, but the server remains the reference. Reinstallation, device changes or cleared storage must not automatically create another charge. def test_timeout_restart_and_retry_produce_one_charge(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TimeoutError):
            self.c.pay('intent1', 90000, 'merchant', True)
        self.assertEqual(self.c.state('intent1'), 'unknown')

blocks.text: The most important adverse scenario has already produced a provider effect. The assertion verifies one charge after reopening the client and repeating the call. Another test permits two equal purchases with different intents, preventing a protection that indiscriminately blocks legitimate payments.

The suite also checks amount conflicts, changed recipients, repeated timeouts and invalid cents. It does not cover a real network, partner key retention, interest or merchant cancellation. The integration contract must test these behaviors with the provider, especially a late response after the journey has moved to support.

pages.title: Measure ambiguity and confirmed effects

blocks.text: Current rates are unknown. A network exception cannot automatically count as duplication. Confirmation requires linking intents and examining effects while preserving legitimate equal purchases. Complete-correction measurement checks principal and associated charges without assuming that every adjustment is a bank loss.

The experiment begins with shadow intent recovery and failure tests. The canary compares mobile versions and compatible partners while holding authorization policy constant. Any new duplication caused by the control, blocked legitimate payment or lost traceability stops expansion. Conversion alone is insufficient evidence of success.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: A strong case does not prove high ROI

blocks.text: Annual assumptions: 30,000, 60,000 or 100,000 ambiguous intents; confirmed duplication in 0.5%, 1% or 2%; incremental prevention of 30%, 50% or 60%. This yields 45, 300 or 1,200 avoided incidents. I assume R$ 50 in support/reconciliation and R$ 40 in irrecoverable charges per incident, totaling R$ 90. The complaint’s amounts are not used as average bank cost.

Assumed implementation: R$ 180,000; annual operations: R$ 36,000. In the base case, 300 × 90 = R$ 27,000; year one is R$ 27,000 − 36,000 − 180,000 = −R$ 189,000. Break-even requires 2,400 actually prevented incidents in year one. None of these scenarios independently justifies full investment. A smaller correction reused across a platform may have different economics and needs a separate estimate.

blocks.title: Separate flows from losses
blocks.text: Refunded principal is not automatically a bank expense. Operational capacity, absorbed charges and customer money are distinct categories. The real incident supplies neither population frequency nor realized benefit.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: A partner-dependent roadmap

blocks.text: The key dependency is knowing what the partner actually guarantees and how long it retains a key. If lookup cannot distinguish pending from absent, the design must preserve that ambiguity. The 90-day schedule is proposed planning, not a commitment by Nubank or its provider.

The EM negotiates integration, testing and support capacity; the Staff Engineer documents guarantees for each failure scenario. Mobile delivery must wait for the server contract. Better wording without state recovery can merely conceal the issue. The economic gate is explicit too: start with a limited change when scenarios do not support a new platform.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: Operate uncertainty without repetition

blocks.text: The canary needs an unknown-intent queue with age, partner and next step. Alerts carry authorized investigation references rather than complete payment data. Payments owns the effect, integration owns the external contract and support owns continuity of customer communication.

The runbook starts by looking up existing intent and provider evidence. It does not tell an operator to create another charge to see whether it works. Late confirmation must update the same case and prevent duplicate correction. A refund request requires its own authorized workflow; it is not an automatic consequence of timeout.

Rollback disables the new experience but preserves recorded intents and confirmations. I would simulate response loss, duplicate callbacks, reordered responses and unavailable lookup. I would also test recovery after app reinstallation. The stopping condition is any scenario in which the displayed state induces a financial action incompatible with what is known.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: My contribution to the contract

blocks.text: As Staff, I would make local guarantees and external dependencies explicit. I would reject exactly-once as a slogan for the entire journey. The design must identify transaction boundaries, deduplication and uncertainty. I would also define retry versus new intent so duplicate prevention does not obstruct legitimate purchases.

As Engineering Manager, I would coordinate mobile, payments, partner and support around reproducible failure scenarios. The team needs time for exercises and reconciliation, not merely a visual delivery target. I would put project cost and evidence of incidence into the same prioritization decision.

The rejected alternative is automatically blocking any payment with the same amount and recipient within a short window. That rule can create false positives and does not solve response loss. Identified intent offers a more precise contract when the partner cooperates. Where it does not, that limitation must remain visible in the design and operational plan.

chapters.subtitle: Provenance, revision and accessibility before assuming an accounting defect
chapters.source_title: Reclame AQUI — refund not perceived in the statement

pages.title: 11 · Visible credit, disputed balance

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: In complaint 213597411, dated 31 March 2025, the customer described three refunds whose sum seemed correct but whose deduction from the bill was unclear. Nubank said they were correctly applied and explained purchases minus early payments minus refunds. The customer confirmed resolution on 8 April. The source establishes neither an accounting defect nor the specific action that resolved it.

blocks.title: Chapter scope
blocks.text: Investigate understanding and read consistency. Individual amounts are not public. The proposal does not presume withheld money; it starts with explaining every credit and its corresponding balance.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: A correct total can remain opaque

blocks.text: Customers need to recognize the original purchase, identify all associated credits and understand the difference between an open balance and a closed document. Three green rows do not necessarily explain how much the amount due changed. The proposal is a navigable calculation breakdown with explicit links between refund, purchase and statement revision.

The falsifiable hypothesis is that decomposition reduces interpretation errors when credit has already been correctly recorded. I would test concrete tasks: finding the canceled purchase, adding partial refunds and explaining the balance after an early payment. If participants still struggle, I would investigate language, grouping or revision discrepancies rather than automatically blame customer attention.

There is also an accounting boundary: a presentation model cannot correct the ledger to make its sum look consistent. The financial source retains authority. The app should demonstrate the calculation for the queried revision and offer investigation when it cannot reconcile it. Closing documents and open views need reference dates without promising identical values across different periods.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Total and detail share a revision

blocks.title: Credit with origin and an explainable balance
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: Events preserve ledger identity and revision. The aggregator links refunds to purchases and builds a snapshot whose total and detail share one revision. Customers can expand the explanation without receiving a second sum computed by independent rules.

Canonical lookup handles missing or inconsistent data; it is not permission to mix values from different revisions. The interface indicates when the reference changes. The design does not cover interest, currency exchange or every entry in a real product; these require integration with financial authority.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Core: identity and refund boundaries

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_11.py; an in-memory model with a local lock.

blocks.text: Each entry has immutable identity. A refund must reference an existing purchase, and principal refunds cannot exceed that purchase in the model. Identical retries do not create a second reduction. A snapshot returns a tuple of immutable objects.

That boundary is deliberate: additional compensation, interest and other categories need their own types rather than a disguised oversized refund. The laboratory has no disk persistence or distributed consumption. The lock demonstrates exclusion within one local authority; a real service needs an equivalent transaction or conditional write.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: One shared sum function

blocks.code:
(defn explain-statement [entries]
  (let [sum-kind (fn [kind]
                   (reduce + (map :cents
                     (filter #(= kind (:kind %)) entries))))
        purchases (sum-kind :purchase)
        refunds (sum-kind :refund)
        payments (sum-kind :payment)
        signed (- purchases refunds payments)]
    {:purchases purchases
     :refunds refunds
     :payments payments
     :amount-due (max 0 signed)
     :credit-balance (max 0 (- signed))}))
blocks.caption: Illustrative, unexecuted Clojure; simplified rules equivalent to the laboratory.

blocks.text: The reducer separates purchases, refunds and payments. When the signed balance is negative, it presents a statement credit balance rather than a negative amount due. This preserves financial meaning when the visible payable total is bounded at zero. Both quantities remain reconcilable.

App, PDF and support should consume the same projection or a shared calculation contract with an explicit revision. Copying the formula across three clients increases divergence risk. Real implementation must add accounting-approved categories and cross-channel parity tests. The function does not decide posting dates or whether a merchant actually returned funds.

def test_three_refunds_reduce_exactly_once(self):
        for i, cents in enumerate((3333, 3333, 3334)):
            refund = Entry('r' + str(i), 'refund', cents, 'p')
            self.s.append(refund)
            self.s.append(refund)
        result = explain(self.s.snapshot())
        self.assertEqual(result['refunds'], 10000)
        self.assertEqual(result['amount_due'], 0)
        self.assertEqual(result['revision'], 4)

    def test_old_snapshot_does_not_change_after_new_credit(self):
        old = self.s.snapshot()
        self.s.append(Entry('r', 'refund', 5000, 'p'))
        self.assertEqual(explain(old)['amount_due'], 10000)
        self.assertEqual(explain(self.s.snapshot())['amount_due'], 5000)
blocks.caption: Literal excerpts; 9 local tests passed.

blocks.text: The synthetic split 3,333 + 3,333 + 3,334 demonstrates exact conservation of 10,000 cents. Replaying each credit leaves the result unchanged. An old snapshot stays stable after a new refund, explaining why two legitimate revisions can display different balances.

Other tests reject missing purchase provenance, excess refund, identity conflict and invalid cents. The concurrency test attempts two 6,000 refunds against 10,000 and accepts only one. Real contractual rules, closing, tax and interest are not tested. These limits should be visible before using the example as an implementation reference.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Success means demonstrated understanding

blocks.text: Baselines are unknown. The experiment uses equivalent tasks and comparable groups with the same financial calculation. It measures accuracy and time without confusing a faster screen with better understanding. Screen readers must announce sign, value and linkage; color cannot be the sole signal of credit.

Contact classification is audited so a financial error is not mislabeled as customer confusion. The canary stops for sum divergence, mixed revisions or worse understanding among assistive-technology users. Detail clicks indicate use rather than success. Final validation asks participants to explain the balance in their own words.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Economics depend on avoided questions

blocks.text: Annual assumptions: 200,000, 500,000 or 1 million eligible refunds; 0.005, 0.015 or 0.025 fewer interpretive contacts per refund; R$ 16 per contact. Assumed implementation: R$ 120,000; operations: R$ 24,000/year. The calculation values support capacity, not credit returned to the customer.

In the base case, 500,000 × 0.015 × 16 = R$ 120,000. After operations and implementation, year one is −R$ 24,000. Break-even requires 600,000 refunds equivalent to the base assumption. If the product already has a common projection, incremental investment may be lower; the estimate must be redone without automatically carrying over the assumed benefit.

blocks.title: Do not count the same journey twice
blocks.text: Exclude duplication contacts covered in case 10 and allocation contacts in 09. Released hours become cash only through concrete spending changes. This study has observed no Nubank incidence rate or saving.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: A calculation-and-language roadmap

blocks.text: The 90-day period is a planning assumption. Representative examples of partial refunds, payments and closing are needed first, using authorized access or synthetic data. Without that coverage, an attractive screen may work only for the simple case and fail on the journey that generates contact.

Staff defines revision and invariants; accounting approves semantics; design validates language; the EM protects research and iteration capacity. Acceptance is not a checklist of rendered components. Customers must recognize credit origin and understand balance, while support reproduces the explanation using the same reference.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Operations with an identifiable fallback

blocks.text: The projection first runs in shadow and compares sums with the financial reference. During the canary, calculation detail appears on demand for a limited cohort. If revision changes during lookup, the interface announces the update and recomputes the complete set rather than replacing only the total while retaining old details.

Alerts cover orphan credits, excess principal refunds and cross-channel revision divergence. The projection team investigates processing; accounting resolves semantics; support distinguishes questions from errors. Logs carry references rather than complete purchase descriptions or personal documents.

Rollback hides the new breakdown and retains the canonical balance, preserving IDs for investigation. An exercise should simulate repeated events, refund arrival before purchase and an older PDF revision. Reconciliation must explain why an event was rejected or awaited a dependency. A credit must never be silently discarded because it arrived out of order.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: My contribution to trust in the sum

blocks.text: As Staff, I would define a financial representation preserving sign, origin and revision. I would avoid three independent calculations for app, PDF and support. The technical choice is an explainable projection with a canonical source and explicit out-of-order policy, without making the interface a financial authority.

As Engineering Manager, I would organize delivery with accounting, experience, accessibility and operations. I would reserve time to observe users interpreting difficult scenarios, because understanding does not automatically emerge from a correct table. The backlog would cover language and support as well as processing and telemetry.

I would reject solving the issue solely by changing refund color or adding an applied badge. That strengthens a claim without making it verifiable. The tradeoff is enough detail without overwhelming the initial screen: a simple summary, progressive explanation and a total rigorously linked to revision. These are proposed contributions, not claims of previous work at the bank.

blocks.text: A reviewer should explain why a credit reduces balance and why an old revision remains different. The solution does not depend on hiding history or teaching customers to manually redo every accounting calculation. The laboratory demonstrates a small contract that product and accounting can discuss.

Proceed only if the projection reconciles, language improves understanding and assistive guardrails hold. Financial error requires ledger correction first. If the issue is interpretive, an experiment can validate a smaller improvement. The case is stronger when it respects that distinction, including the fact that the historical complaint was resolved.
