pages.title: From my experience to the team’s stack.

rows: Paired reviews of code and incidents.

blocks.text: Joining a new organization means learning how it makes decisions. I would start with one complete flow: from the gesture in the app to the service, event, persistence, and support. From there, I would identify what is standard, where exceptions exist, and which commitments were made to sustain current operations.

The functional lab included in this edition demonstrates that approach. It runs in Clojure and separates state transformation from external effects. This does not replace experience with the internal platform; it narrows the distance between saying I learn a language and showing an artifact that can be reviewed. The same standard applies to management: explain how I would learn from the team before promising reorganization.

blocks.title: The first delivery I would aim for
blocks.text: A small, observable, reversible improvement built with people who know the domain. The initial objective is to earn context and trust through the work.

pages.chapter_title: Wesley Vieira · a proposal for Nubank

blocks.text: The functional core receives one state and returns another. An invalid transition produces an explicit error; it does not call a network, queue, or database. This separation allows the contract to be discussed before infrastructure is chosen. Within the model, versioning prevents an old intent from changing a newer state.

blocks.code:
(def transitions
  {:received #{:pending :rejected}
   :pending #{:settled :rejected}
   :settled #{}
   :rejected #{}})

(defn advance [db key expected-version next-status]
  (let [{:keys [status version] :as current} (get db key)]
    (when-not current
      (throw (ex-info "unknown operation" {:reason :not-found})))
    (when-not (= expected-version version)
      (throw (ex-info "stale writer" {:reason :version-conflict})))
    (when-not (contains? (get transitions status #{}) next-status)
      (throw (ex-info "illegal transition"
                      {:reason :illegal-transition})))
    (assoc db key (assoc current :status next-status
                         :version (inc version)))))
blocks.caption: Excerpt from decision_core.clj; local execution verified. In-memory model without networking.

blocks.text: The excerpt is part of decision_core.clj, executed in Clojure 1.12.0 on Java 17. The complete file has 11 tests and 22 assertions. Value immutability provides neither durable persistence nor distributed exclusion: when integrating a database, version comparison and writing must share the same atomic boundary.

pages.title: Clojure: repetition does not create another intent.

blocks.text: The idempotency key identifies intent; the fingerprint identifies its relevant content. Repeating the same key with the same value preserves state. Reusing it with a different value is a conflict, not a new purchase. In the synthetic example, key scope is the in-memory database; production would need customer, operation, and retention policy.

blocks.code:
(defn register [db {:keys [key amount currency] :as cmd}]
  (when-not (valid-command? cmd)
    (throw (ex-info "invalid command"
                    {:reason :invalid-command})))
  (let [fingerprint [amount currency]
        existing (get db key)]
    (cond
      (nil? existing)
      (assoc db key {:fingerprint fingerprint
                     :status :received :version 0})
      (= fingerprint (:fingerprint existing)) db
      :else
      (throw (ex-info "key reused with different payload"
                      {:reason :key-conflict})))))

;; Em um único processo: atualização atômica do modelo.
;; Nunca adicionar efeitos externos à função de swap!.
(def state (atom {}))
(swap! state register
       {:key "synthetic-001" :amount 1250 :currency :BRL})
blocks.caption: Excerpt from the local lab; valid-command? is defined in the complete file. Concurrency test executed.

blocks.text: The concurrency test submits eighty identical registrations against an atom and verifies one entry. This exercises local atomicity; it does not demonstrate exactly-once processing between services. Production still needs authenticated identity, persistence, expiration control, reconciliation, and a consistent response when the connection drops after commit.

The model separates operation identity from state evolution. The identity constraint prevents the same operation being represented as two entities. Version compare-and-swap accompanies the status change in the transaction. This is an educational proposal, not a description of Nubank's schema.

blocks.code:
;; Schema proposto para um exercício de domínio.
[{:db/ident :operation/id
  :db/valueType :db.type/uuid
  :db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one
  :db/unique :db.unique/identity}
 {:db/ident :operation/status
  :db/valueType :db.type/keyword
  :db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one}
 {:db/ident :operation/version
  :db/valueType :db.type/long
  :db/cardinality :db.cardinality/one}]

;; Uma transação propõe a mudança de versão e status.
;; entity-id e expected-version são obtidos pelo adapter.
[[:db/cas entity-id :operation/version
  expected-version (inc expected-version)]
 [:db/add entity-id :operation/status :operation/pending]]
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: A correct version alone does not guarantee a valid business transition. The adapter must validate the state machine and ensure the observed condition belongs to the authorized transaction. History helps explain decisions but requires retention policy and care not to persist unnecessary sensitive data. Exact semantics depend on the edition and API the team adopts.

The proposed envelope carries event identity, aggregate identity, and domain version. Each answers a different question: have I processed this delivery, which operation does it belong to, and where does it fit in the sequence? The consumer must not confuse a transport offset with a business version.

blocks.code:
{
  "event_id": "synthetic-event-001",
  "event_type": "operation.status_changed",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "aggregate_id": "synthetic-operation-001",
  "aggregate_version": 2,
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z",
  "producer": "proposed-operation-service",
  "correlation_id": "synthetic-correlation-001",
  "payload": {
    "previous_status": "pending",
    "status": "settled",
    "currency": "BRL",
    "amount_minor": 1250
  }
}
blocks.caption: Proposed JSON contract with synthetic identifiers; not an internal Nubank event.

blocks.text: The partition key must reflect the unit for which order matters. Reprocessing a message requires idempotency in the effect, not just the producer. A Kafka transaction does not automatically turn an external call or a write to another database into a single global transaction. The relevant test interrupts the consumer between persistence and acknowledgment and observes recovery.

pages.title: AWS / DynamoDB: arbitrate the first write.

blocks.text: A conditional reservation makes key creation a competition resolved by storage. A service must not perform query-then-insert as two independent operations and assume exclusivity. Scope prevents a customer's key from being confused with another intent.

blocks.code:
# Exemplo de adapter com boto3; cliente e tabela são externos.
# Nomes e valores são sintéticos.
def reserve(table, scope, request_key, fingerprint):
    pk = f"IDEMPOTENCY#{scope}#{request_key}"
    return table.put_item(
        Item={
            "pk": pk,
            "fingerprint": fingerprint,
            "status": "reserved",
            "version": 0,
        },
        ConditionExpression="attribute_not_exists(pk)",
    )

# Uma ConditionalCheckFailedException exige consultar
# o registro: replay compatível ou conflito de payload.
# Não converter todo erro em 'já processado'.
# A expiração da chave precisa respeitar a janela de replay.
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: Reservation is not settlement. If the process crashes after reserving and before submitting the operation, pending work must be distinguished from completed work. Reserved state needs recovery with ownership and a time bound. Expiration policy must not allow a late retry to repeat a financial effect already performed.

The example reserves capacity for one additional replica while gradually removing the previous version. Readiness should indicate whether an instance can receive work; it must not fluctuate with every shared-dependency failure and remove the entire service simultaneously. The numbers are educational assumptions.

blocks.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: proposed-journey-reader
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: journey-reader}
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate: {maxUnavailable: 0, maxSurge: 1}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: journey-reader}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: reader
          image: example.invalid/reader:replace-with-reviewed-digest
          ports: [{containerPort: 8080}]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /ready, port: 8080}
            periodSeconds: 5
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: "250m", memory: "256Mi"}
            limits: {memory: "512Mi"}
blocks.caption: Reference manifest, deliberately without an executable image. Not applied to a cluster.

blocks.text: Before applying it, a reviewed image, service identity, network policies, graceful shutdown, concurrency limits, and distribution across zones would be required. Three replicas in the same failure domain do not fail independently. Rollout must observe journey completion and saturation as well as count ready pods.

The component receives domain state; it does not infer completion from an absent spinner. A pending message must remain true when the network fluctuates. The design avoids offering retry while the financial outcome remains unknown; the next action depends on the reconciliation contract.

blocks.caption: Reference Flutter/Dart excerpt; not compiled in this edition.

blocks.text: The example needs widget, screen-reader, text-scaling, and real-navigation tests. A live region can announce a change without moving focus, but excessive announcements also harm the experience. Final wording should be developed with Design and Content, including expected time, a safe action, and a help channel when the delay is no longer normal.

pages.title: Dart: states that do not contradict one another.

blocks.text: A collection of booleans can represent impossible combinations: loading and completed, no receipt and available. A closed set of states makes these possibilities more visible. Here, a confirmed receipt requires its own identifier; query unavailability is not presented as an operation failure.

blocks.caption: Educational Dart 3 example; not compiled in this edition.

blocks.text: Typing helps implementation, but the server remains authoritative for financial state. The client must handle old contract versions and unknown responses. Fallback should preserve confirmed data without inventing a new success state. The proposal must be validated against the team's Dart version and modeling conventions.

Numerator and denominator must observe the same population. If abandoned journeys disappear from instrumentation, latency can look better while the experience gets worse. The measurement contract must define start, completion, timeout, legitimate cancellation, and missing events.

blocks.caption: Proposed PromQL queries; not executed on a Prometheus server.

blocks.text: Aggregated percentiles require care with buckets and distributions. A percentile alone reveals neither volume nor success rate; it must be read alongside counts, errors, and segmentation. Labels need bounded cardinality. Account, operation, and customer identifiers belong in controlled diagnostic trails, not time-series labels.

A trace should explain relationships between operations, not merely enumerate calls. Payment confirmation can cross synchronous and asynchronous stages, retries, and reconciliation. Sampling must retain enough failure and high-latency examples for investigation.

blocks.code:
# Fragmento de instrumentação; tracer fornecido pelo runtime.
def confirm(command, repository, tracer):
    with tracer.start_as_current_span("journey.confirm") as span:
        span.set_attribute("journey.kind", "payment")
        span.set_attribute("contract.version", 1)
        try:
            result = repository.confirm(command)
            span.set_attribute("journey.outcome", result.kind)
            return result
        except TimeoutError:
            span.set_attribute("journey.outcome", "unknown")
            raise

# Não registrar CPF, token, saldo ou payload integral.
# Propagar contexto entre produtores e consumidores.
# Para processamento assíncrono, modelar links/parentesco
# de acordo com a semântica real do trabalho.
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: A trace does not replace a durable financial record. It may be sampled, delayed, or missing precisely during an incident. Diagnostics should associate an operation with a trace through controlled access while keeping personal data out of common attributes. The goal is shorter investigations without creating another indiscriminate repository of sensitive information.

A timeout for each dependency can add up to more time than the journey allows. A shared budget forces every stage to account for time already consumed. A monotonic clock suits duration within a process; distributed timestamps require another contract and tolerance for clock differences.

blocks.caption: Reference Java excerpt; not compiled as a program in this edition.

blocks.text: Canceling a wait does not undo a remote effect. After a timeout, the outcome may remain unknown and require reconciliation. This is where my JVM experience connects to the financial domain: controlling threads and connections is necessary, but retry decisions depend on idempotency, authority, and state. The example is not a complete HTTP client.

pages.title: Python: an experiment must be allowed to fail.

blocks.text: Python can quickly make a behavioral hypothesis concrete. A useful test describes an observable consequence, such as blocking expansion when the sample is insufficient. The code example is a deterministic gate, not a statistical significance test. The threshold must come from an approved journey policy.

blocks.caption: Educational example separate from the twenty executed labs; synthetic threshold.

blocks.text: The twenty case labs use synthetic data and local tests. They help detect contract regressions, illegal states, and representation errors. They do not measure Nubank's infrastructure, estimate real load, or certify production controls. Each chapter records exactly what the lab covers and what requires additional validation.

The schema makes certain invariants impossible to ignore accidentally: positive amount, supported currency, and a unique key per scope. The update conditions the transition on state and version. If no row returns, the service must distinguish conflict, replay, and a nonexistent identifier.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE proposed_operation (
  operation_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_scope TEXT NOT NULL,
  request_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount_minor BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_minor > 0),
  currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL CHECK (currency = 'BRL'),
  version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (version >= 0),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
    status IN ('received','pending','settled','rejected')
  ),
  UNIQUE (customer_scope, request_key)
);

UPDATE proposed_operation
SET status = 'pending', version = version + 1
WHERE operation_id = $1
  AND version = $2
  AND status = 'received'
RETURNING operation_id, version, status;
blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: PostgreSQL is an educational option in this book, not an inference about every Nubank domain's database. A status constraint limits vocabulary but does not express the complete state machine. Transaction, indexes, isolation, and outbox strategy must be evaluated together so persistence and publication recover coherently from failures.

Cache policy starts with a product question: how much delay can this data tolerate? An informational projection may accept brief validity; financial authorization may require the authoritative source. The same tool can be appropriate for one path and unsuitable for another.

blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: TTL bounds duration but does not prevent a late write from reinstalling an older version. Distributed implementation needs version comparison, invalidation, or another workload-appropriate strategy. The example deliberately omits that mechanism and identifies it as remaining work. Redis is a proposed alternative, not a claim about Nubank's internal design.

Infrastructure as code makes decisions available for review: ownership, recovery, resource identity, and protection against accidental removal. Someone capable of assessing impact must interpret the plan; it should not be approved merely because the file passed formatting.

blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: prevent_destroy replaces neither access control nor backup policy. Removing the configuration block or changing the management strategy requires additional care. The example was not applied and includes no remote backend, provider version, managed key, or IAM policy. These omissions are explicit so an editorial excerpt does not look production-ready.

A static type does not validate JSON received at runtime. The proposed parser treats the boundary as unknown and rejects states outside the contract. In a product, rejection must become a safe experience with an alternative query or incompatibility message, without inventing financial confirmation.

blocks.caption: Independent reference example; not executed against real infrastructure.

blocks.text: TypeScript is used here for contracts and visualization, not as a general Nubank requirement. For a real SDK, I would generate types from a versioned schema, maintain fixtures for old consumers, and define handling of additional fields. Safe evolution expands the contract without forcing every client to update simultaneously.

pages.title: Grafana: a dashboard that guides action.

blocks.text: The dashboard starts with the decision someone needs to make. Confirmed completion, unknown state, and reconciliation age describe different aspects of trust. CPU and memory aid diagnosis but do not independently demonstrate that the customer completed the task.

blocks.caption: Conceptual dashboard specification; not Grafana's import schema.

blocks.text: The JSON is an editorial specification, not an importable Grafana dashboard. Each indicator needs a definition, denominator, window, owner, and connection to the response procedure. Red without an agreed action creates noise. A good dashboard also displays missing data and small samples so telemetry silence is not interpreted as success.

blocks.title: One journey, two authorities.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: The architecture separates the authority that changes state from the authority that presents it. The domain core and its storage decide whether an operation was accepted. The projection makes reading easier, but carries version and lag. A screen cannot turn a missing update into rejection, and support cannot promise reversal without consulting the state responsible for the effect.

The outbox represents publication intent within the same boundary as the domain write. A publisher may repeat messages, so the consumer must deduplicate effects. The design allows failures between stages and makes recovery part of the contract. The choice between Datomic, DynamoDB, or another persistence option depends on the domain and existing platform; all three are not added simultaneously for aesthetic reasons.

The Clojure lab demonstrates only the in-memory decision. The case labs explore specific properties. Distributed integration, authorization, retention, and capacity still require validation in the team's context.

pages.title: Recovery as part of the product.

blocks.title: Recovery as part of the product.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: Recovery should not be a collection of ownerless exceptions. The flow must distinguish technical inability, suspected fraud, and insufficient evidence. Each may require a different path. Human review belongs where it adds judgment, not as an unlimited destination for every integration error.

The record associates decision, policy, and validity. An old signal must not authorize a sensitive action indefinitely. When an alternative is denied, the product must explain the next available step without disclosing details that help bypass controls. This language requires collaboration between Security, Product, Content, and Support.

Success combines legitimate resolution, recovery time, and protection. Reducing a queue by rejecting more people can improve an operational metric while worsening the outcome. As EM, I would ensure capacity and responsibilities; as Staff, I would define authority, expiration, and review mechanisms.

blocks.title: An experience platform with contracts.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: A server-driven interface platform increases composition speed, but also increases the importance of its contract. The installed client may lag behind the server version. The validator must understand the renderer's minimum capability and prevent a configuration requiring nonexistent behavior.

Fallback is a product component: it must preserve the task and accessibility, not merely prevent crashes. Telemetry connects configuration, app version, and journey outcome. The gate requires sufficient evidence before expanding exposure. The decision retains an owner; it is not delegated to one context-free metric.

Nubank publishes work on BDC; this design is an educational proposal for discussing governance and evolution. I would investigate existing controls and seek the smallest necessary extension. The platform creates value when it reduces consumer-team effort while maintaining quality and recovery capability.

blocks.title: ML: separate prediction from decision.
blocks.caption: Independent reference design. Does not represent Nubank's internal architecture.

blocks.text: A score is not a business decision. Policy combines prediction with limits, context, and review paths. Separating these responsibilities allows a threshold to change without pretending the model was retrained and supports investigation into whether the problem lies in data, inference, or use of the result.

Features need identity and time: what was available when a decision was made may differ from what we know today. Evaluating with future information creates an impression of quality that would not exist in production. The training-serving contract must prevent this leakage and measure relevant differences.

Ground truth may arrive late and remain incomplete. Experiments must preserve version trails and treat false positives as legitimate people harmed by a decision. The proposed value is to improve protection and recovery together, with specialists responsible for policy and exposure criteria.

blocks.title: Resolved historical case · RA 250462257
blocks.text: On June 3, 2026, a customer reported receiving BRL 700.00, transferring BRL 200.00 and attempting another BRL 300.00 Pix that failed. More than 24 hours later, she said the money had not returned. On June 9, Nubank acknowledged a localized communication issue, reported an automatic refund and a privately supplied statement. On June 10, she marked the complaint resolved and rated support 9. The exact refund time is not public.

The product question is whether a failed transfer lets a person distinguish the attempt, temporarily unavailable money and a confirmed return. The private statement was not inspected, so this chapter does not reconstruct a balance or a financial timeline beyond the report. The capture documents a public complaint and subsequent resolution; it is not a customer app screen or evidence of a current defect. The proposal preserves that outcome while examining a possible ambiguity in the journey.

sources.title: Reclame AQUI — public complaint and response

blocks.text: A falsifiable hypothesis is that return information reaches the query channel after financial confirmation, extending uncertainty without necessarily extending the hold. I would correlate the attempt, confirmation, posting and first visible query, accounting for clocks and versions. If the information was already available and understood, the hypothesis weakens; investigation moves to presentation or support context.

The team would distinguish transport failure, rejection before settlement and an actual refund. These are different events. The public response identifies no service, database or queue, so attributing this episode to Kafka, caching or distributed architecture would be unsupported. The first deliverable is a map of observed states and owners, not an infrastructure replacement.

Investigation must also separate client time from server time. An attempt may be created offline, sent later and queried from another device. Without this distinction, a dashboard attributes connectivity delay to financial confirmation. I would use timestamps with declared provenance and a per-operation timeline under restricted investigative access. Clock discrepancies should appear as measurement uncertainty rather than negative durations silently discarded. This also makes comparisons between app versions more credible and prevents an apparently faster path from merely using a different clock.

blocks.title: BRL 300.00 Pix: clarify the refund
blocks.caption: Independent proposed architecture; suggested technologies, not Nubank internal infrastructure.

blocks.text: The authenticated entry queries the domain, which applies only authorized transitions. The durable record keeps event identity and confirmed state in one transaction. The help path provides guidance without creating another financial instruction.

Asynchronous publication can lag, so the read model declares its latest confirmation and has a reconciliation path. The design does not move authority over money into the interface. The lab verifies a local boundary without simulating settlement in the Pix scheme.

blocks.code:
def confirm(self, op, event_id, target, trusted=False):
        if trusted is not True or not event_id:
            raise PermissionError("verified adapter required")
        allowed = {"pending": {"settled", "refund_pending"},
                   "refund_pending": {"refunded"}}
        with self.connect() as db:
            db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            prior = db.execute("SELECT op,target FROM events WHERE id=?",
                               (event_id,)).fetchone()
            if prior:
                if prior != (op, target):
                    raise ValueError("event identity conflict")
                return False
            row = db.execute("SELECT state,amount FROM ops WHERE id=?",
                             (op,)).fetchone()
            if not row:
                raise KeyError(op)
            if target not in allowed.get(row[0], set()):
                raise ValueError("illegal transition")
            returned = row[1] if target == "refunded" else 0
            db.execute("UPDATE ops SET state=?,returned=? WHERE id=?",
                       (target, returned, op))
            db.execute("INSERT INTO events VALUES (?,?,?)",
                       (event_id, op, target))
            return True
blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from the executed independent lab; remaining validation is in the complete file.

blocks.text: An operation starts pending. A failure confirmation allows it to await a refund; only a subsequent authorized event marks the return. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes writers in the educational SQLite file. Event identity is compared with its payload, preventing the same key from representing another transition.

The returned amount is recorded in cents and never increases on replay. Ten queries do not change the state. This defines the guarantee: the model records confirmation rather than deciding to return money after a timeout. Signature verification, adapter authenticity and ledger reconciliation remain required integrations.

blocks.text: The Clojure example makes the transition rule inspectable and separates rejection from side effects. In production it must operate on a still-valid version inside an appropriate transaction or with version comparison. A correct pure decision does not eliminate races between reading and writing.

I would start with the existing stack. Choosing PostgreSQL or Datomic depends on the owning domain, transaction mechanisms already operated and migration cost. The Flutter UI would consume explicit states, with copy reviewed so that “awaiting confirmation” does not become “money lost.” This Clojure excerpt was not executed.

def test_concurrent_refund_replays_once(self):
        self.apply("failed", "refund_pending")
        barrier = threading.Barrier(4)
        def retry(_):
            barrier.wait(timeout=5)
            return self.apply("refund", "refunded")
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(retry, range(4)))
        self.assertEqual(results.count(True), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.bank.read("pix-a", "owner-a")[
            "returned_cents"], 30000)

    def test_timeout_is_not_refund_authority(self):
        for _ in range(10):
            self.bank.read("pix-a", "owner-a")
        receipt = self.bank.read("pix-a", "owner-a")
        self.assertEqual(receipt["state"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual(receipt["returned_cents"], 0)

blocks.text: The 12 executed tests cover four concurrent consumers, replay, payload conflict, authorization, invalid money and reopening the file. Repeated queries ensure the application does not hide a financial decision inside a read. The rejected-transition test verifies that an event identity is not consumed before a valid effect exists.

These tests do not validate signed messages, power failure, participant availability or production capacity. Before a pilot, I would add replay of anonymized real messages and publisher recovery tests. The required evidence is preservation of identity and amount, not merely an HTTP 200 response.

The experiment begins with shadow queries compared against the financial source, without displaying the new receipt. An eligible cohort then receives the explanation while the control retains the previous experience and the same support access. The analysis unit is an unresolved attempt, so retries are not counted as additional customers.

Collection combines confirmed events and support contacts through restricted references, never through a customer’s public text. I would observe each attempt for seven days and segment by app version and failure path. Any false confirmation, cross-account access or duplicate Pix attributable to the receipt stops expansion. The baseline is unknown and must be measured.

BRL 300.00 is the principal discussed in the complaint; it is not bank profit and does not enter this calculation. The scenarios assume 20,000 / 50,000 / 100,000 eligible attempts per month, incremental contact reductions of 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.15 and an avoidable marginal cost of BRL 8.00 per contact. Assumed additional monthly operating costs are BRL 4,000.00 / BRL 8,000.00 / BRL 15,000.00.

The calculation is volume × contacts avoided per attempt × marginal cost, less operations. The assumed BRL 120,000.00 investment pays back only when monthly net contribution is positive. The conservative scenario shows that a useful idea may not fund its implementation within the first year at that scale. Released capacity without lower expenditure must be reported as capacity; average salary is not a substitute for marginal cost.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 120,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL 48,000.00 / BRL 384,000.00 / BRL 1,260,000.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

The 90-day horizon is a proposal conditional on discovery. The Pix technical owner validates states and evidence; product approves interpretation; support checks that it can explain the same receipt. The EM coordinates dependencies and specialist availability without assuming authority over financial rules.

I would not move directly from design to a broad cohort. The intermediate gate requires reconciling a sample of attempts and proving that a lost response remains queryable later. If the main observed cause is an actual refund delay, the work must include the corresponding financial domain; changing copy alone would be insufficient. The budget can be revised after that diagnosis.

Rollout starts with the observer, then authenticated querying and finally presentation. A flag can remove the new screen but must not delete recognized receipts or events. During rollback, the previous service must still query a compatible record; incompatible versions must be stopped before receiving traffic.

The payments on-call owner receives divergence alerts while support receives approved guidance for unknown states. A drill injects duplicate events, publication lag and unavailable reads. The safe response preserves evidence and initiates reconciliation rather than issuing another transfer. Alerts without an owner or a resolution procedure do not satisfy operational acceptance.

As Staff, I would propose the authority boundary, review invariants and document the choice between querying a projection and reaching the financial source. I would also facilitate review with the owning teams to reduce unnecessary dependencies. The rejected alternative is a timer that turns silence into a refund: it confuses unavailability with a financial decision and may contradict settlement that already occurred.

As EM, I would organize small deliveries, investigation capacity and a shared definition of done involving support and product. These are proposed contributions, not claims that I already led this initiative at Nubank. An interview can explore how I would negotiate reduced scope that preserves correctness when a commercial deadline favors an apparently faster solution.

In an interview, I would ask for an anonymized unresolved attempt and explain which decision each additional piece of evidence would enable. This demonstrates reducing ambiguity before choosing technology. As a leader, I would identify who can authorize a financial-contract change and who owns the customer message. Collaboration prevents a local improvement from merely transferring uncertainty to another team. The result should be a decision record that another engineer can challenge and operate, rather than a design whose correctness depends on its author remaining available.

blocks.title: Historical incident resolved · July 8, 2026
blocks.text: On July 8, 2026, Canaltech reproduced a Pix sent to Nubank that did not appear in the app. Its test between Nubank accounts did not reproduce the problem. The report described an account-loading notice. Nubank reported temporary instability and recovery around 11:15. The transferred amount, affected population and exact duration were not published.

The evidence combines a newsroom’s own observation with the bank’s response. This is more specific than a mention count but does not replace financial telemetry. The article photograph shows the application’s store listing, so its caption is editorial. It is not presented as an error screenshot. The article quotes posts on X that were not individually verified at their origin. This chapter uses the reported observation and recovery without estimating losses.

A missing displayed balance permits different hypotheses: unavailable reads, a delayed projection, interrupted integration or an unconfirmed credit. I would begin with the latest known confirmation at each layer without assuming ledger failure. Cross-institution and internal Pix transfers are different probes; the published sample does not establish that only external transfers were affected.

The testable hypothesis is that an old snapshot remained visible without enough validity context. Testing requires source version, source time, query time and displayed message. If the source itself has not confirmed the credit, the product should express uncertainty rather than turn a refreshed screen into financial certainty. Support needs to distinguish these situations.

A snapshot version must be comparable within one account and a defined source. Adding versions from different components creates an artificial order. If a summary combines multiple sources, the response needs coverage and age for each relevant component. I would start with the smallest set that explains the displayed balance rather than turning this case into a rewrite of the entire home screen. This boundary makes correctness demonstrable before broadening composition and gives product a concrete choice about which information remains useful during partial failure.

blocks.title: Incoming Pix, stale balance
blocks.caption: Independent proposed architecture; suggested technologies, not Nubank internal infrastructure.

blocks.text: The financial source remains authoritative. The validator accepts increasing versions, and the projection stores validity alongside the amount. Reconciliation compares samples with the origin and returns only confirmed corrections.

Journey status combines two independent facts: freshness of that balance and presence of an incident. Closing a banner does not renew the snapshot. This separation avoids a green interface that conveys confidence without new financial evidence.

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from the executed independent lab; remaining validation is in the complete file.

blocks.text: BalanceView.read checks the account holder and clock before building the response. Without a snapshot it returns unknown with an absent amount; zero would be a false financial assertion. A time preceding the observation also yields unknown. At the exact validity boundary, the state becomes stale.

The model permits displaying the last amount with its timestamp but never recommends resending Pix. Its lock protects one process’s memory only. Persistence, authentication and clock synchronization must be implemented outside this core. Integer seconds simplify testing without prescribing the real API’s time format.

blocks.caption: Proposed integration example, not executed; this is not Nubank internal code.

blocks.text: In the proposed Dart example, a presentation function treats unknown, stale and fresh as explicit states. Incident status arrives separately. The visual layer neither computes balance nor changes validity; it translates contracts into understandable, accessible information.

I would check assistive-technology reading, localized time and reconnection behavior. An endless skeleton can hide an earlier balance; showing that amount without context can mislead. The decision requires comprehension research using real tasks. The example was not compiled, and its messages require product review before use.

Validity duration must reflect the data contract and be configured by the financial owner rather than chosen arbitrarily by the UI. blocks.text: The 14 tests challenge time boundaries, version conflict, unauthorized sources, another account and concurrent publication. The key test lets the banner expire while the balance remains old. Another publishes versions out of order and requires the highest to survive. Testing whether a message appears is insufficient: amount, version and context must remain coherent.

The program does not establish distributed-clock quality or external-system freshness. Integration would add clock-skew simulation, partial reads and delayed probes, alongside accessibility testing. The 12,000-cent fixture is synthetic and does not come from the report.

Collection must separate availability, correctness and freshness. A fast endpoint can return old data; a healthy probe does not represent every originating bank. I would segment by receiving path and app version, using aggregate volumes and a rolling 15-minute operations window.

A communication experiment must compare equivalent incidents or cohorts because severity varies. The hypothesis is fewer contacts and repeated attempts without hiding uncertainty. Expansion stops for a balance labeled current without valid evidence, an amount discrepancy or unsafe retry guidance. I would not set a latency target before measuring the existing path.

The modeled cost concerns incident handling, not supposedly lost money. Monthly assumptions are 2 / 3 / 4 comparable incidents, 20,000 / 40,000 / 60,000 sessions per incident and incremental contact reductions of 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.03. Each avoidable contact hypothetically costs BRL 7.00; probes and operations add BRL 5,000.00 / BRL 8,000.00 / BRL 12,000.00 per month.

I multiply incidents × sessions × contact-rate difference × cost and subtract operations. Hypothetical implementation investment is BRL 150,000.00. These volumes are sensitivity inputs, not estimates of the July event. Results cannot be transferred automatically to an incident of different severity. The same session must not be counted in both this case and case 01 to add benefits.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 150,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL -26,400.00 / BRL 105,600.00 / BRL 460,800.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

During the first weeks, financial engineering and reliability define what each source confirms. Product and support agree on messages for absence, lag and recovery. The probe owner verifies that probes create no unauthorized transfers and do not congest the real path.

The next milestone is an invisible comparison between calculated labels and evidence. Only then does a small cohort receive the interface. The EM coordinates review and on-call coverage; Staff resolves source, projection and client contracts. If freshness cannot be measured reliably, launch remains limited to unavailability guidance rather than simulated precision.

The runbook separates query failure from absent financial confirmation. If the observer loses connectivity, it must not announce that every Pix failed. An incident has an owner, scope, version and expiration; a recovery update must be traceable to its owner.

In the failure drill I freeze the projection, expire the banner and restore only the API. The UI must still recognize old data. Rollback removes new messages while retaining snapshots and instrumentation. Support receives an answer consistent with the technical view and is not instructed to confirm a credit the system has not confirmed.

Lab limitation: incident notices are unversioned, so an old notice can replace a newer one. This does not refresh the balance. Notice ordering belongs to the proposed integration and is not implemented in this example.

My Staff contribution would make validity semantics explicit and review how the client receives a composite response. I would reject a single “system normal” boolean because it mixes global health, local availability and correctness for one account. A richer representation requires product care but explains limits without inventing certainty.

As EM, I would lead a delivery involving reliability, payments, mobile and support with named accountable roles. Stopping can be valuable: a banner that creates confusion or false confirmations should not expand even if it reduces calls. I would bring evidence and alternatives to the team while respecting its decisions and existing stack expertise.

A sound Staff decision also makes the observer’s unknowns explicit. I would discuss with product the difference between reporting unavailability and claiming that an operation did not happen. As EM, I would protect post-incident analysis time and review alert usefulness with the people carrying the pager. This routine reduces pressure to publish a green status without sufficient evidence merely to close an administrative incident. It also gives support a reliable escalation path when the global message and one customer’s experience do not agree.

blocks.title: Outcome reported by the press · March 2026
blocks.text: Metrópoles reported that more than BRL 2,000.00lion belonging to a beauty business was blocked on January 20, 2026, followed by account closure. The article attributes a tax-refund origin to the defense and reports a court order. Nubank cited security and compliance and declined case details on confidentiality grounds. In the March 11 video, the reporter said the money was transferred to another bank. Court records and compliance were not independently verified.

The article and transcript make different contributions. The article describes the dispute; the 06:59–07:23 transcript adds the outcome according to the reporter. I do not claim to have watched the entire video or inspected court records. This proposal does not treat the restriction as current. It also does not transfer compensation from other customers in the article to this episode. The case informs review, explanation and exit design with controls appropriate to each decision’s authority.

blocks.caption: Actual frame from Metrópoles, 11 March 2026. The transcript describes the company case at 02:26 and reports release at 06:59–07:23.

blocks.text: The technical question is whether a restriction remains connected to grounds, evidence, an owner and its next review as it crosses support, risk and account closure. This does not determine whether a particular suspicion was valid. A testable hypothesis is lost context between initial restriction and execution of an authorized exit.

I would sample cases by measure type and reconstruct state changes with accountable owners. Decision time would be compared with actual transfer instruction, distinguishing document waits, active legal holds and operational queues. The report does not provide that breakdown. I would not apply a universal 72-hour deadline: the rule depends on the relevant grounds and requires legal validation.

A document submitted by a business may be relevant without being conclusive. The system must record receipt, reviewer and the authorized decision arising from it rather than automating a legal conclusion because a file exists. I would also investigate handoffs: a support task marked complete does not necessarily close risk review. Distinguishing work status from restriction status prevents productivity indicators from hiding operationally unresolved cases. Each transition should expose its prerequisite to the next owner so that progress does not depend on reconstructing a conversation from scattered messages.

blocks.title: Account restriction: review and exit
blocks.caption: Independent proposed architecture; suggested technologies, not Nubank internal infrastructure.

blocks.text: Review receives events and consults the effective policy. An eligible decision proceeds to financial execution while the trail retains grounds and communication. The customer receives only approved status information, without antifraud thresholds or third-party data.

The design separates review from execution. Approving an exit does not prove that the balance was transferred. Confirmation depends on reconciliation, an authorized destination and no active impediments, checked again at the execution boundary.

blocks.text: Restriction.execute_exit requires an executor role, expected version, destination ownership, reconciled balance and explicit clearance of active impediments. Each rejection preserves the prior approval without transferring money. The review clock does not authorize execution: an overdue date creates pending work, not technical permission to move funds.

The 200,000,100-cent amount is merely a synthetic fixture above BRL 2,000.00lion, not the case’s exact amount. This model uses an in-memory lock and makes no payments. Real integration requires durable transactional control, operator identity and transfer confirmation by an authorized financial domain.

blocks.text: The 14 tests show that overdue review does not release money, failed reconciliation blocks execution and a reviewer does not automatically hold the executor role. They also cover another owner’s destination, missing evidence, stale version, replay and invalid values. A second execution cannot increase the transferred total.

The suite does not validate a policy’s legal correctness or document authenticity. The next level requires role-integration tests and simulation of a new restriction arriving between approval and sending. The goal is to prove that operational simplification creates no unauthorized release while retaining an auditable path for eligible cases.

Queue age must be segmented by grounds; mixing a document request with a court order can hide distinct priorities. The dashboard measures cases without an owner or scheduled review and tracks approval-to-confirmed-execution time. Individual case data remains restricted.

I would compare equivalent cohorts by category and complexity while preserving human review. Fewer contacts are beneficial only if they do not result from obstructed appeals. Unauthorized release, exposure of detection signals or unreconciled execution immediately stops the pilot. Baselines and operating limits must be set with risk, legal and operations rather than inferred from the reported amount.

The calculation does not treat held funds as a benefit. Assumptions are 1,000 / 2,500 / 4,000 monthly reviews, 10 / 15 / 20 minutes saved per review and BRL 90.00 per hour. Only 25% / 40% / 50% of released capacity is assumed to become avoidable expenditure. Monthly operations of BRL 5,000.00 / BRL 10,000.00 / BRL 18,000.00 and a hypothetical BRL 180,000.00 implementation are deducted.

The formula is cases × minutes / 60 × hourly cost × realizable share, less operations. That share must be demonstrated through an actual spending change; without it, the corresponding financial benefit is zero even if the queue improves. Avoided compensation is excluded because no verifiable causal probability or cost supports it.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 180,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL -15,000.00 / BRL 150,000.00 / BRL 504,000.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

Planning begins with a taxonomy of measures and named legal and operational owners. Architecture follows understanding where each team’s authority ends. A closed account needs an exit path as explicit as the path that created its restriction.

Staff coordinates contracts and revalidation points; the EM secures legal, risk and support capacity at acceptance milestones. Shadow mode must reproduce previous decisions without executing them. Cases with unapproved grounds or no owner remain outside the pilot until resolved. The horizon is proposed rather than a commitment made by Nubank.

The initial canary covers a small set of restriction types and does not automate the substantive decision. Overdue-review alerts go to category owners; execution-divergence alerts go to the financial domain. Customers receive stage information rather than a calendar-based promise of release.

The operations drill includes a new restrictive order after approval, changed destination ownership and failure after sending an instruction. In the latter case, query and reconciliation precede any resend. Rollback freezes new executions through the new version and preserves audit history. A faster queue that loses grounds, evidence or appeal access is unacceptable.

As Staff, I would help turn implicit states into a traceable protocol for appeals, review and execution. The rejected alternative is automatic release when a timer expires. It appears to solve delay but ignores active impediments and confuses a work deadline with financial authority.

As EM, I would organize specialist collaboration without promising that engineering alone can decide a regulatory question. This includes review capacity, support training and stopping criteria backed by accountable owners. My proposed value is connecting technical quality with operational responsibility, not presenting this external proposal as a past achievement.

In a leadership assessment, I would explain how to handle tension between customer urgency and a restriction that remains valid. The response is permitted information, accountable review and correct execution when authorized. I would ask the team to discuss an edge case and record its decision, including why a particular step should remain manual. This makes the project reviewable by specialists beyond engineering and avoids implying that faster software can substitute for the authority or evidence needed to make a substantive decision.

blocks.title: Resolved · RA 230743513
blocks.text: On October 31, 2025, a customer reported being unable to access the account because facial authorization depended on a broken camera. On November 3, Nubank said it had received a selfie with a code, internally validated the device and enabled its features. The customer marked the problem resolved. The source does not disclose exact duration, unavailable funds or how the alternative photo was captured.

This case does not establish a facial-recognition error. The reported barrier is physical inability to capture an image, and the response shows an assisted solution already existed. The proposal improves discovery, routing and tracking of that alternative without claiming Nubank lacked it. There is no public biometric photograph to reproduce; the capture documents the complaint and resolution. The technical discussion begins when repeating the same instruction is no longer useful.

sources.title: Reclame AQUI — public complaint and response

blocks.text: Denied permission, unavailable camera and unconfirmed identity are different reasons. Combining them in a generic message creates attempts that do not change device capability. The hypothesis is that diagnosing the barrier before capture reduces repeated routing while retaining the same identity requirement.

I would investigate local error sequences, attempts and contacts per journey without storing images in analytics. A sample of assisted recoveries would reveal where people abandon or restart. If routing is already clear and waiting occurs in specialist analysis, priority shifts to review capacity and quality. The complaint alone does not measure that distribution.

Local diagnosis must be treated as an untrusted signal. A modified client can declare that no camera exists, so this result only selects a guidance path and never lowers identity requirements. I would also investigate whether the alternative is usable by someone without another device, keeping that limitation explicit in research. The resolved case does not identify what enabled alternative capture, so the same option cannot be assumed for everyone. Accessibility review should examine actual available resources rather than treating successful completion by one person as universal usability.

blocks.text: The person submits evidence through a protected channel while policy determines acceptable alternatives. Review produces a decision bound to the challenge and intended device. Policy can also revoke the record before consumption.

The authorizer does not interpret a photograph or a support message; it consumes a valid approval once. The interface declares recovery only after authorization is confirmed. People and reviewers are roles, not branded software components.

blocks.text: Recovery.authorize requires binding to the holder, device and challenge, plus a valid deadline and prior approval. Completion consumes the challenge and prevents reuse. Invalidation occurs under the same lock as precondition checking, so two concurrent calls cannot authorize using the same local evidence.

The code neither recognizes faces nor decides whether a person is legitimate. review receives an identity decision already validated by a trusted adapter in the model. This boundary matters: testing a state machine does not prove biometric security. Production evidence, operators and sessions need appropriate authentication and persistence.

I would review accessibility from the first screen: predictable focus, spoken instructions and preserved progress after interruption. The alternative should not require discovering a support contact through trial and error. blocks.text: The 14 tests verify single use under concurrency, exact expiration, a different device, wrong holder, revocation, missing evidence and misleading truthy values. The most important test confirms that declaring a camera problem authorizes nothing. Another shows that an incorrect challenge does not make a later attempt succeed without review.

Real capture, liveness, accessibility and storage tests are still missing. Those belong to different layers with their own criteria. I would add network-interruption and device-change drills during recovery, checking that an approved decision remains bound to the correct context rather than moving to another device.

Legitimate completion and account takeover must be read together. Higher conversion that authorizes the wrong people is a regression even if support volume falls. Collection segments physical barriers, permissions and review without making raw biometrics an analytics dimension.

The pilot retains a comparable cohort of eligible journeys and observes repeat contacts for seven days, plus fraud signals over the identity team’s chosen window. Comprehension testing includes people with capture limitations. Any confirmed increase in unauthorized access stops expansion; longer review time also requires checking whether the flow merely moved work to specialists.

Assumptions are 3,000 / 8,000 / 15,000 monthly recoveries, 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6 contacts avoided per journey and BRL 9.00 per contact. The alternative may add review: assume 0.10 / 0.08 / 0.05 additional reviews per journey at BRL 18.00. Operations add BRL 3,000.00 / BRL 6,000.00 / BRL 10,000.00 monthly, with hypothetical implementation of BRL 110,000.00.

The formula deducts additional review before operations. Better routing is therefore not automatically cheaper. No customer balance enters the calculation because none was published. Residual fraud must be measured as a guardrail and budgeted if an attributable difference exists; no unsupported antifraud benefit is assumed. Support capacity becomes cash savings only when realizable spending falls.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 110,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL -36,000.00 / BRL 135,360.00 / BRL 690,000.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

The first milestone aligns identity, mobile and accessibility on alternatives already available. The second instruments barrier reasons without collecting sensitive material. The third builds resumability and tracking in a controlled environment. Only then does a pilot measure whether people reach the correct channel with fewer repeated attempts.

The EM must reserve human-review capacity before increasing intake. Staff defines binding and revocation contracts with device owners. More routing without review capacity can worsen waiting, so acceptance covers queue quality rather than screens alone. The proposed timeline may change after discovery.

Rollout does not begin by disabling facial recognition. It begins by making an approved alternative discoverable and trackable. Identity on-call receives alerts for repeated use, mismatched context and consumption failures; support is instructed not to request material through improvised channels.

Drills include a challenge expiring during review, holder revocation and approval followed by connection loss. Resumption queries existing state before opening another case. Rollback preserves decisions and retains previous assisted channels. If evidence-to-device binding is uncertain, the response is renewed authorized review rather than release for convenience.

As Staff, I would separate device capability from identity confidence so a UI simplification cannot contaminate authorization. I would reject a rule accepting any photograph after a camera error: a physical problem does not make evidence more trustworthy. A sound alternative requires policy, review and single-use binding.

As EM, I would coordinate mobile, identity, privacy and support around a journey the organization can operate. This includes specialist capacity and training as well as code. My proposed contribution makes security and accessibility joint quality criteria while remaining transparent about what the lab demonstrates and what requires further validation.

I would also avoid a conversion target that pressures reviewers to approve uncertain cases. The EM should track decision quality, workload and escalation while Staff keeps the protocol capable of representing waiting and additional review. Recovery may legitimately take longer when evidence is missing. The desired improvement removes unproductive repetition and improves guidance while preserving the security decision the case requires. That distinction helps a team discuss tradeoffs honestly and prevents a convenient completion metric from becoming the only definition of success.

blocks.title: Answered · RA 242544191
blocks.text: On March 6, 2026, a customer reported changing phones, not knowing or accessing the previous email and receiving no code at a newly supplied address. On March 13, Nubank explained additional checks and said a device had been authorized on March 9. It was awaiting a reply to private guidance. The record is answered, with no public final confirmation from the customer. The cause of delivery failure is unproven.

An authorized device does not by itself prove that the person completed the entire reported journey. The response may indicate meaningful progress, but it does not turn answered into resolved. This case concerns email, not SMS or a broken camera. Private messages were not inspected. The proposal uses the reported barrier to examine the contract between updated contact, delivered code, validated code and a new-device session.

sources.title: Reclame AQUI — public complaint and response

blocks.text: The report supports investigation of delivery, generation binding and journey comprehension, but identifies no provider, bounce or spam filter. I would trace a recovery_id across change request, issuance, provider acceptance, delivery feedback and validation. SMTP acceptance means neither reading nor identity proof.

One hypothesis is that the customer cannot distinguish the active contact from the challenge that remains valid after resending. Logs and research can refute this: if contact and challenge are consistent, the bottleneck may lie elsewhere. I would not claim a root cause from a “did not arrive” message alone.

Delivery investigation must acknowledge incomplete feedback. Some providers report acceptance without delivery confirmation; others produce delayed or duplicated events. I would document which signals are observations and which are inferences, keeping customer messages consistent with that distinction. A newly supplied address still requires identity validation before changing account contact. Research should observe whether people understand that confirming contact and recovering access can require different steps. Otherwise, a technically accurate delivery message may create the false expectation that the account should already be available.

blocks.text: The versioned contact feeds issuance and verification. Policy sets limits while the record retains the current challenge. The verifier rechecks generation before consuming a code, preventing a concurrent change from leaving an old challenge usable.

The app receives contact progress separately from access. Confirming an address is only one step; device authorization remains in the identity domain. The diagram does not treat the delivery provider as an authority on account ownership.

A simple hash of a short code is insufficient against database extraction; appropriate secret and key design is required. The purpose is lifecycle and binding verification rather than a production-ready authentication service.

blocks.text: The 14 tests cover contact change with an old code, resend, attempt limits, expiration, future clock, replay and wrong holder. The state-separation test confirms that email validation does not authorize a device. This invariant prevents a delivery mechanism from becoming complete identity proof.

The suite sends no email and measures no deliverability. Provider events, cross-process limits and timing-based enumeration tests remain missing. Before production, I would add coordinated resend attacks and two sessions changing contact concurrently, plus integration with the real identity-recovery policy.

The funnel must show issuance, observable delivery, contact validation and authorization without treating them as equivalent. I would measure repeat contacts per recovery and time per stage, segmented by provider and app version where volume is sufficient to preserve privacy.

The experiment compares eligible journeys of similar complexity and observes legitimate recovery, messages sent and review load. Better delivery accompanied by more abuse does not pass acceptance. Expansion stops for accepted obsolete codes, account-data leakage or account takeover attributable to the flow. Baselines remain unknown until instrumentation and identity-team validation.

Assumptions are 10,000 / 30,000 / 60,000 monthly journeys, repeat-contact reductions of 0.05 / 0.12 / 0.18 and BRL 8.00 marginal cost per contact. Additional messages are 15,000 / 45,000 / 90,000 at BRL 0.03 each, plus BRL 4,000.00 / BRL 7,000.00 / BRL 12,000.00 monthly operations. Hypothetical implementation costs BRL 100,000.00.

Net benefit is journeys × avoided repeat contacts × cost, less messages and operations. Global average revenue per customer is not used to value recovered access; that would require causal incremental revenue and margin evidence unavailable in this complaint. The conservative scenario may be negative, showing that sending more messages without sufficiently reducing confusion does not justify investment through avoided cost.
Assumed implementation budget: BRL 100,000.00. Annual net results before implementation: BRL -5,400.00 / BRL 245,400.00 / BRL 860,400.00. Every input is an assumption, not a Nubank baseline.

The roadmap starts with an inventory of available events and contact-recovery methods. Identity validates which changes require review; the delivery owner explains what callbacks actually mean. Product defines progress messages that do not reveal account data.

Shadow mode compares issued and consumed generations before changing resend or experience. The EM coordinates provider dependencies and review capacity; Staff resolves concurrency and policy persistence. If observability reveals a predominantly external problem, the plan should prioritize the adapter and communication instead of unnecessarily rebuilding authentication.

During canary rollout, old and new issuers must share generation control. A UI flag cannot stop an incompatible backend from accepting an old code. Migration requires compatibility or explicit exclusion of versions that do not understand the new identity.

The drill includes late delivery feedback, concurrent resend and contact change while a code is in transit. Operations must distinguish provider delay from an already-revoked challenge. Rollback preserves generations and limits rather than reactivating old secrets. Abuse alerts go to identity; aggregate delivery failures go to the channel owner.

As Staff, I would propose generation binding and the separation between contact possession and device authorization. I would reject accepting any unexpired code: two contacts and two resends can leave several contradictory proofs apparently valid. The challenge must be current in the correct context.

As EM, I would organize delivery across security, messaging and mobile, including abuse tests in the definition of done. I would also ensure support sees the same progress without accessing secrets. These are proposed technical and coordination actions, not claims of authority or prior results inside Nubank.

The technical decision must withstand pressure to remove steps without understanding their purpose. I would explain which controls are necessary for risk and which repetitions result only from poorly preserved state. As EM, I would organize a support review using anonymized journeys so the people receiving customer questions participate in design. This produces a more operable solution and avoids adding another resend button without fixing context. The review should end with concrete examples of what the interface can truthfully say at each stage and when a specialist must intervene.

blocks.text: An “under review” state may be blocking every edit even though adding evidence and changing the original claim carry different risks. This is a hypothesis, not a proven app cause. I would map internal stages and external deadlines to identify where additional evidence can still be considered.

Investigation compares upload attempts, contacts requesting submission and analyst decisions. It must distinguish UI restrictions, format limits, quarantine and network cutoffs. If material was already outside the applicable deadline, improvement may mean an explanation and an allowed route rather than implying engineering can unilaterally reopen the dispute.

I would also distinguish supplementary evidence from correcting the disputed transaction itself. The former may be appended without changing case identity; the latter may require reviewing the object of the dispute. If both use one generic edit button, it becomes difficult to explain what was actually received. The proposed design records submission intent and traceability so an analyst can determine its relationship to earlier material. This avoids treating every later document as either a harmless addition or an unauthorized change when its meaning requires judgment.

def test_late_evidence_is_retained_without_submission_promise(self):
        item = self.upload(now=101)
        self.d.scan(item["version"], True, True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.d.submit(item["version"], "dispute-analyst", True)

The suite does not validate real file types, antivirus, accessibility or network rules. I would add malformed-file and interrupted-upload tests, plus restoring the relationship after a temporary URL expires.

Success is not simply more attachments. The main metric tracks eligible material received with a receipt and reviewed within a useful window. More irrelevant documents can increase cost and delay decisions, so analyst time and admissibility must also be observed.

The pilot compares disputes at similar stages and with similar reasons, reviewed by analysts familiar with deadlines. Repeat contacts are measured per dossier over seven days. No chargeback result is attributed to the improvement without an appropriate comparison because merit and merchant behavior affect outcomes. As Staff, I would propose immutable additional evidence rather than freely reopening the entire form. This preserves the original claim and makes changes auditable. The rejected alternative is overwriting the earlier attachment: it simplifies the screen but loses context and may confuse review.

As EM, I would coordinate dispute operations, mobile, security and privacy, placing analyst capacity and training in the same plan as development. The proposed contribution turns a concrete barrier into an operable flow without promising chargeback success or attributing financial results to a code example.

A hiring discussion can explore how I would negotiate minimum scope with operations: the first gain may be a receipt and routing before automated submission. As Staff, I would document that boundary to reduce risk; as EM, I would ensure the team is not held accountable for a network outcome it does not control. The commitment would cover intact receipt, review within the applicable window and correct information, measured separately from financial victory. pages.title: Diagnosis before design

blocks.text: Diagnosis separates interbank progress from message delivery to the customer. Missing email does not reveal whether a case is under analysis, rejected, unfunded or affected by a communication failure. The engineering hypothesis is that explicit states and a next update reduce uncertainty-driven contacts.

I would reconstruct received events, available projection and emitted notifications per case without inferring that delay caused the receiving account to be emptied. The source does not demonstrate that causality. The episode occurred in 2025; a current implementation must map 2026 contracts and rules with Pix, risk and legal rather than judging historical conduct against later requirements.

The timeline should explain partial recovery without turning the remainder into a debt owed by the bank. It must also distinguish operational closure from definitive impossibility of any future recovery under the applicable contract. I would not fill event gaps with a probable outcome merely to simplify the screen. When information is unconfirmed, the next action is investigation and communication of the limitation, preserving the ability to update state when authorized evidence arrives. This makes uncertainty visible without inventing either a positive or negative financial promise.

pages.title: Observed access does not settle consent

blocks.text: The engineering question starts at the boundary between evidence and conclusion. A record of an authorized device may matter to an investigation, but it should not be stored as a synonym for the account holder’s intent. This proposal separates access facts, the policy version applied, the reviewer’s interpretation and the communicated decision. A customer can then challenge a specific premise without restarting the entire conversation.

The falsifiable hypothesis is that some rework comes from incomplete dossiers or decisions whose reviewable reasoning is unclear. I would compare an authorized sample of cases with repeat contacts against what the agent could see at that time. If dossiers were already complete and understandable, the hypothesis weakens; the intervention may belong in policy, communication or another stage.

The study does not propose publishing fraud-control secrets or refunding every disputed loan. Financial decisions remain subject to approved authority and policy. The objective is consistent analysis with an owner, minimized evidence and a defined appeal. Legal and operational complexity requires specialist validation before setting deadlines or interim measures.

blocks.code:
def test_appeal_requires_independent_reviewer(self):
        self.seed()
        self.d.append('a', 2, 'owner', 'customer', 'appeal', {})
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionError):
            self.d.append('r', 3, 'r1', 'reviewer', 'review', {'policy': 'v2'})
        self.assertEqual(len(self.d.history()), 3)
        self.d.append('r', 3, 'r2', 'reviewer', 'review', {'policy': 'v2'})
        self.assertEqual(self.d.history()[1]['evidence']['policy'], 'v1')

    def test_restart_and_retry_preserve_one_evidence(self):
        self.d.append('e', 0, 'a', 'analyst', 'evidence', self.ev)
        self.d.close()
        self.d = Dispute(self.path)
        result = self.d.append('e', 0, 'a', 'analyst', 'evidence', self.ev)
        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
        self.assertNotIn('consent', result[0]['evidence'])
blocks.caption: Literal excerpts; the complete local suite passed 9 tests.

blocks.text: The first assertion protects appeal independence and verifies that rejection does not change history. The second closes and reopens the database, retries an action and confirms a single record. Other tests attack stale revisions, incorrect roles, missing evidence and sensitive payloads.

Tests do not assess human quality, evidence authenticity or policy fairness. Production work would add blinded sample review, cross-account access tests, permission expiry, export auditing and tool-outage exercises. A system that perfectly preserves a poor decision still needs process correction.

pages.title: Measure useful review and human effort

blocks.text: The baseline is unknown. I would instrument transitions with pseudonymized case_id, revision and timestamp; work time requires operational sampling rather than queue duration alone. Case age and actual effort are different measures. Unauthorized access and audit failures are additional guardrails.

The pilot would compare equivalent teams or periods using predefined eligibility, avoiding selection of easy cases only. Independent reviewers would assess samples from both groups. Expansion would stop for data exposure, lost evidence or a material deterioration in decision consistency, even if average handling time improved.

pages.title: Value: recovered capacity, not profit

blocks.text: Every input is assumed: 12,000, 24,000 or 40,000 annual dossiers; 8, 14 or 18 rework minutes saved; R$ 90 fully loaded hourly cost. Valued capacity is N × minutes ÷ 60 × 90. Implementation is assumed at R$ 240,000 and annual operations at R$ 60,000, 90,000 or 120,000. The final column subtracts both in year 1 and does not represent realized cash.

In the base case, 24,000 × 14 ÷ 60 × 90 = R$ 504,000; subtracting R$ 90,000 and R$ 240,000 leaves R$ 174,000 in modeled net capacity. Year-one break-even requires approximately 15,715 equivalent dossiers. Redistributing hours does not automatically save cash. Investment depends on confirming avoidable rework and identifying a concrete use for the released capacity.

blocks.title: Keep financial categories separate
blocks.text: Disputed principal and possible fraud are excluded. Loss estimates require verified exposure, confirmation and recovery. Do not aggregate benefits with other chapters that cover the same contacts.

pages.title: A 90-day plan with accountable roles

blocks.text: The calendar is a planning assumption. The critical dependency is authorized access to a sufficient sample, not building a screen. If evidence sources are incompatible, the first deliverable becomes identifying those gaps and assigning owners to resolve them.

The Engineering Manager coordinates capacity across lending, fraud, support and privacy; the Staff Engineer defines contracts and technical criteria. Policy review remains with its owners. Every phase ends with observable evidence and a recorded decision to continue, narrow or stop. The schedule does not promise changes dependent on external validation.
