pages.title: Operate without abandoning the queue

blocks.text: Deployment starts in shadow mode: the new tool prepares dossiers while the existing operation continues making decisions. Completeness, preparation time and discrepancies are compared without automatically changing collections or credit. The next canary exposes tracking and review to a limited cohort, with human capacity reserved for appeals.

Alerts distinguish aging queues, unavailable evidence and authorization failure. Operations owns queue response; security owns exposure; the service team owns lost or duplicated events. A projection outage neither closes the case nor deletes its trail. Customers receive an honest stage and next action.

Rollback disables the new projection and automatic routing while preserving history and active cases. An exercise should simulate database failure after a decision, permission revocation during access and return of an old revision. The runbook must explain pending-work reconciliation and continuity communication without exporting dossiers to unprotected spreadsheets.

pages.title: My contribution to the decision

blocks.text: As Staff, I would define the evidence model, authorization boundaries and review invariants. I would lead the consistency, retention and signal-exposure discussion using concrete disagreements. The most important decision would be to keep access records separate from interpretation of consent, preventing a technical field from carrying a conclusion it cannot support.

As Engineering Manager, I would establish joint delivery with operations and risk, an end-to-end owner and reserved review time. I would first prioritize the most frequent demonstrated rework, with explicit criteria for choosing product changes, integration or training as the next investment. These are proposed actions, not claims that I have managed Nubank teams or policies.

I would reject automatic refusal merely because the dossier contains a known device. I would also avoid exposing every signal to support. The proposal balances useful review with minimized access and accepts higher operational effort when needed to protect the quality of a sensitive decision.

pages.title: 09 · Paid does not explain allocation

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: Complaint 242838873, dated 10 March 2026, describes a statement marked paid while credit was not fully restored, after three support tickets. On 17 March, Nubank reported correcting the statement, recognizing the payment and settling advanced installments. It explained credit restoration through processing and financed balances. The public status is Responded; no final customer confirmation is visible. Individual amounts are masked.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The response reports a correction but does not expose the ledger, event order or technical cause. This study proposes allocation traceability rather than diagnosing the responsible system.

pages.chapter_title: Paid statement, uncertain credit: follow every cent

pages.title: Three states, different consequences

blocks.text: Receiving money, applying money and refreshing a credit-limit view are separate stages. An interface can correctly report a payment while leaving unanswered which obligations were settled. With financing, the effect on available credit depends on rules that a single label cannot explain. The receipt must connect receipt of funds, destination and consequence rather than merely replace a word on screen.

My hypothesis is that some repeat contact comes from the absence of this verifiable link across channels. Investigation would use the payment identifier to reconstruct confirmation, allocations, compensating entries and projection updates. I would compare what the customer saw against support and ledger records at the same revision. If obligation calculation is wrong, improved presentation is insufficient and financial correction takes priority.

The responsibility boundary includes contractual financing rules and settlement recognition. The app cannot independently choose where to move money. It should also avoid inviting a second payment while the first allocation is uncertain. The proposal makes the pending state explicit and provides tracking under the same identifier.

pages.title: A receipt linked to the ledger

blocks.title: Verifiable allocation and versioned reading
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The allocator receives financial confirmation and applies a validated plan. The canonical receipt and its projection share a revision. The reconciler compares receipt values against independent invariants; a discrepancy is not solved by hiding cents in presentation.

Available-credit updates may run at a different pace, but must expose their revision and state. The diagram summarizes responsibilities, not every integration. Financial correction requires authorized compensating entries in the ledger; the reconciler detects and routes discrepancies without independently editing balances.

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_09.py; SQLite represents one local authority.

blocks.text: The conditional write prevents applying more than an obligation owes. Allocations and receipt share a transaction: if the second destination is invalid, the first returns to its prior state as well. Unapplied funds remain explicit.

The example receives a preselected plan and does not implement Nubank’s contractual priority. Production selection requires versioned policy, account authorization and settlement evidence. A retry is accepted only when amount and plan are identical. Reusing the key to change destination requires a different authorized action, never a silent update.

(defn allocation-valid? [{:keys [received allocations unapplied]}]
  (and (pos-int? received)
       (every? pos-int? (vals allocations))
       (<= 0 unapplied)
       (= received (+ unapplied (reduce + (vals allocations))))))

(defn allocation-event [payment-id revision plan]
  {:event-type :payment-applied
   :payment-id payment-id
   :revision revision
   :allocations plan})
blocks.caption: Illustrative Clojure example, not executed; the Python laboratory is the tested artifact.

blocks.text: The function checks conservation but cannot prove that each obligation is eligible. That validation belongs inside the transactional boundary that knows balance, account holder and contract. Separating pure calculation from persistence helps test rules and review changes without attributing database guarantees to the function.

Event integration should persist allocation and publication intent atomically. The projection consumer deduplicates by identifier and financial revision. Transport ordering alone is insufficient: replay, reprocessing and consumer changes can redeliver the same fact. Publication failure leaves identifiable pending work, not permission to apply the payment again.

blocks.code:
def test_failure_after_first_write_rolls_everything_back(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.l.apply('p', 20000, {'bill': 10000, 'installment': 6000})
        self.assertEqual(self.l.due('bill'), 10000)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.due('installment'), 5000)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.db.execute(
            'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM allocations').fetchone()[0], 0)

    def test_restart_retry_does_not_apply_twice(self):
        first = self.l.apply('p', 12000, {'bill': 10000})
        self.l.close()
        self.l = Ledger(self.path)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.apply('p', 12000, {'bill': 10000}), first)
        self.assertEqual(first['unapplied'], 2000)
        self.assertEqual(self.l.due('bill'), 0)
blocks.caption: Literal suite excerpts; 9 tests passed.

blocks.text: The partial-failure test attempts to settle one obligation and exceed another, verifying full rollback. The recovery test reopens the database and confirms that the same receipt cannot apply money twice. The suite also checks a residual cent, conflicting plan, fractional amount and payment against an already settled obligation.

Interest, fees, currency, reversals and cross-account authorization remain outside scope. An integration test should observe outbox and projection after failure between commit and publication, checking the receipt against an independent source. Local conservation is necessary but does not replace settlement-system reconciliation.

pages.title: A financial case with two cost components

blocks.text: Every input is hypothetical: 60,000, 120,000 or 240,000 eligible payments/year; 0.06, 0.10 or 0.14 fewer contacts per payment; R$ 18 per contact. I additionally assume 1, 2 or 3 reconciliation hours saved per thousand payments at R$ 100/hour. Implementation: R$ 260,000; annual operations: R$ 60,000. Contacts and reconciliation hours must represent different work.

The base case is 120,000 × 0.10 × 18 + 120 × 2 × 100 = R$ 240,000 in annual capacity. Year one is R$ 240,000 − 60,000 − 260,000 = −R$ 80,000. Break-even requires 160,000 payments equivalent to the base assumption. This supports a pilot or reuse of components rather than automatic approval of the full project.

pages.title: A reconciliation-led roadmap

blocks.text: The main dependency is a trustworthy financial reference against which to compare the new view. Without it, a dashboard can merely make an error more persuasive. In the first phase, accounting and credit approve examples for partial payments, financing, anticipation and compensation, with amounts in cents and explicit revisions.

pages.title: Rollback preserves financial writes

blocks.text: Launch starts with shadow reading. The projection calculates a receipt and compares it with the ledger without guiding customers or changing allocations. A canary then exposes the allocation explanation to eligible accounts. The old view remains an identified fallback, without mixing total and detail revisions.

Alerts combine unapplied-fund age, projection delay and sum violations. Platform owns publication; credit and statements own financial interpretation; operations coordinates customer resolution. An error queue should carry IDs and reasons rather than unnecessary complete financial data in broadly accessible logs.

Disabling the new receipt does not undo confirmed payments. Rollback affects presentation and routing, followed by reconciliation of pending work. Exercises include crashes before and after commit, a delayed consumer and concurrent correction. Throughout recovery, the tool must distinguish received from applied money for customers and support alike.

pages.title: My contribution on two fronts

blocks.text: As Staff, I would center the design on conservation and identity. I would choose the transaction boundary, define compensation and document which reads may be eventually consistent. I would reject inferring available credit from a paid-statement label because it replaces a financial contract with a visual approximation.

As Engineering Manager, I would bring together teams that may see different parts of the same payment. I would establish an end-to-end resolution owner and an investigation agreement using shared IDs. The plan must include support training and exception-handling capacity, not only a mobile component.

I would also advocate an economic decision proportional to the evidence. The base scenario does not recover implementation cost in the assumed first year. If an existing receipt API can be extended, the cost changes and must be recalculated. My role is to expose that tradeoff and protect journey integrity without presenting potential capacity as realized savings.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: Timeout is not definitive failure

blocks.text: An interruption can occur after a partner accepts payment but before the app receives confirmation. During that interval, saying that nothing happened can induce another financial intent. This chapter hypothesizes that an explicit unknown-outcome state, paired with lookup of the original attempt, reduces unintended repetition without preventing legitimate new purchases.

Investigation must reconstruct identifiers, timestamps and contracts across client, service and provider. Retrying one intent must be distinguished from a deliberate second purchase. Amount, merchant and temporal proximity support analysis but are insufficient identity: two equal purchases may be legitimate. The public source cannot establish which mechanism was present or absent in the incident.

Control should begin before dispatch: create and persist intent, bind content to a key and recover state after app restart. If the provider lacks idempotency or reliable lookup, the guarantee weakens. The experience must then acknowledge uncertainty and initiate reconciliation rather than promise exactly one distributed execution.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: One intent crosses uncertainty

blocks.title: Resume the same payment
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The record binds key, amount, currency and recipient before dispatch. The provider retains the same key across attempts. Confirmation and reconciliation update the original intent, allowing the app to recover the receipt after losing the response.

The model uses two databases to represent the service/provider boundary. No distributed transaction spans them. The property explicitly depends on provider deduplication; without that capability, the design requires a different operational strategy and cannot retain the same promise.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: Core: persist before dispatch

blocks.code:
def pay(self, key, amount, merchant, timeout_after_provider=False):
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
            raise ValueError('nonempty intent identity required')
        if type(amount) is not int or amount <= 0 or not merchant:
            raise ValueError('invalid intent')
        payload = json.dumps([amount, merchant])
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            old = self.db.execute('SELECT payload,receipt FROM intents WHERE key=?',
                                  (key,)).fetchone()
            if old and old[0] != payload:
                raise ValueError('intent conflict')
            if old and old[1]:
                return old[1]
            self.db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO intents VALUES(?,?,NULL)',
                            (key, payload))
        receipt = self.provider.charge(key, payload)
        if timeout_after_provider:
            raise TimeoutError('provider committed; local outcome unknown')
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute('UPDATE intents SET receipt=? WHERE key=?',
                            (receipt, key))
        return receipt

    def state(self, key):
        row = self.db.execute('SELECT receipt FROM intents WHERE key=?',
                              (key,)).fetchone()
        return 'absent' if row is None else ('confirmed' if row[0] else 'unknown')
blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_10.py; two local databases and a synthetic provider.

blocks.text: Intent is recorded before the external call. The injected timeout occurs after provider commit but before the local receipt is saved. Recovery uses the same key and receives the existing receipt, demonstrating that missing a response does not authorize another effect.

A local transaction should not remain open while waiting on the network: this creates locks without making the partner an atomic participant. The laboratory exposes that separation. In production, payload includes account scope and contract; integration must address key retention, expiry and provider compatibility.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: State should guide the next action

blocks.caption: Illustrative Dart, not executed; states and copy require product and accessibility review.

blocks.text: The interface offers lookup of the existing attempt when the outcome is unknown. The wording is only an example: it must explain what is being checked without asserting debit or failure before confirmation. A new-purchase button must represent explicit new intent rather than a disguised retry.

Local persistence helps app recovery, but the server remains the reference. Reinstallation, device changes or cleared storage must not automatically create another charge. After session recovery, the client queries authorized recent intents. Recipient information should enable recognition while minimizing sensitive detail and never exposing integration credentials.

pages.title: Measure ambiguity and confirmed effects

blocks.text: Current rates are unknown. A network exception cannot automatically count as duplication. Confirmation requires linking intents and examining effects while preserving legitimate equal purchases. Complete-correction measurement checks principal and associated charges without assuming that every adjustment is a bank loss.

The experiment begins with shadow intent recovery and failure tests. The canary compares mobile versions and compatible partners while holding authorization policy constant. Any new duplication caused by the control, blocked legitimate payment or lost traceability stops expansion. Conversion alone is insufficient evidence of success.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: A strong case does not prove high ROI

blocks.text: Annual assumptions: 30,000, 60,000 or 100,000 ambiguous intents; confirmed duplication in 0.5%, 1% or 2%; incremental prevention of 30%, 50% or 60%. This yields 45, 300 or 1,200 avoided incidents. I assume R$ 50 in support/reconciliation and R$ 40 in irrecoverable charges per incident, totaling R$ 90. The complaint’s amounts are not used as average bank cost.

Assumed implementation: R$ 180,000; annual operations: R$ 36,000. In the base case, 300 × 90 = R$ 27,000; year one is R$ 27,000 − 36,000 − 180,000 = −R$ 189,000. Break-even requires 2,400 actually prevented incidents in year one. None of these scenarios independently justifies full investment. A smaller correction reused across a platform may have different economics and needs a separate estimate.

blocks.title: Separate flows from losses
blocks.text: Refunded principal is not automatically a bank expense. Operational capacity, absorbed charges and customer money are distinct categories. The real incident supplies neither population frequency nor realized benefit.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: A partner-dependent roadmap

blocks.text: The key dependency is knowing what the partner actually guarantees and how long it retains a key. If lookup cannot distinguish pending from absent, the design must preserve that ambiguity. The 90-day schedule is proposed planning, not a commitment by Nubank or its provider.

The EM negotiates integration, testing and support capacity; the Staff Engineer documents guarantees for each failure scenario. Mobile delivery must wait for the server contract. Better wording without state recovery can merely conceal the issue. The economic gate is explicit too: start with a limited change when scenarios do not support a new platform.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: Operate uncertainty without repetition

blocks.text: The canary needs an unknown-intent queue with age, partner and next step. Alerts carry authorized investigation references rather than complete payment data. Payments owns the effect, integration owns the external contract and support owns continuity of customer communication.

The runbook starts by looking up existing intent and provider evidence. It does not tell an operator to create another charge to see whether it works. Late confirmation must update the same case and prevent duplicate correction. A refund request requires its own authorized workflow; it is not an automatic consequence of timeout.

Rollback disables the new experience but preserves recorded intents and confirmations. I would simulate response loss, duplicate callbacks, reordered responses and unavailable lookup. I would also test recovery after app reinstallation. The stopping condition is any scenario in which the displayed state induces a financial action incompatible with what is known.

pages.chapter_title: NuPay after an error message: recover intent before retrying

pages.title: My contribution to the contract

blocks.text: As Staff, I would make local guarantees and external dependencies explicit. I would reject exactly-once as a slogan for the entire journey. The design must identify transaction boundaries, deduplication and uncertainty. I would also define retry versus new intent so duplicate prevention does not obstruct legitimate purchases.

As Engineering Manager, I would coordinate mobile, payments, partner and support around reproducible failure scenarios. The team needs time for exercises and reconciliation, not merely a visual delivery target. I would put project cost and evidence of incidence into the same prioritization decision.

The rejected alternative is automatically blocking any payment with the same amount and recipient within a short window. That rule can create false positives and does not solve response loss. Identified intent offers a more precise contract when the partner cooperates. Where it does not, that limitation must remain visible in the design and operational plan.

pages.title: 11 · Visible credit, disputed balance

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: In complaint 213597411, dated 31 March 2025, the customer described three refunds whose sum seemed correct but whose deduction from the bill was unclear. Nubank said they were correctly applied and explained purchases minus early payments minus refunds. The customer confirmed resolution on 8 April. The source establishes neither an accounting defect nor the specific action that resolved it.

blocks.title: Chapter scope
blocks.text: Investigate understanding and read consistency. Individual amounts are not public. The proposal does not presume withheld money; it starts with explaining every credit and its corresponding balance.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: A correct total can remain opaque

blocks.text: Customers need to recognize the original purchase, identify all associated credits and understand the difference between an open balance and a closed document. Three green rows do not necessarily explain how much the amount due changed. The proposal is a navigable calculation breakdown with explicit links between refund, purchase and statement revision.

The falsifiable hypothesis is that decomposition reduces interpretation errors when credit has already been correctly recorded. I would test concrete tasks: finding the canceled purchase, adding partial refunds and explaining the balance after an early payment. If participants still struggle, I would investigate language, grouping or revision discrepancies rather than automatically blame customer attention.

There is also an accounting boundary: a presentation model cannot correct the ledger to make its sum look consistent. The financial source retains authority. The app should demonstrate the calculation for the queried revision and offer investigation when it cannot reconcile it. Closing documents and open views need reference dates without promising identical values across different periods.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Total and detail share a revision

blocks.title: Credit with origin and an explainable balance
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: Events preserve ledger identity and revision. The aggregator links refunds to purchases and builds a snapshot whose total and detail share one revision. Customers can expand the explanation without receiving a second sum computed by independent rules.

Canonical lookup handles missing or inconsistent data; it is not permission to mix values from different revisions. The interface indicates when the reference changes. The design does not cover interest, currency exchange or every entry in a real product; these require integration with financial authority.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Core: identity and refund boundaries

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_11.py; an in-memory model with a local lock.

blocks.text: Each entry has immutable identity. A refund must reference an existing purchase, and principal refunds cannot exceed that purchase in the model. Identical retries do not create a second reduction. A snapshot returns a tuple of immutable objects.

That boundary is deliberate: additional compensation, interest and other categories need their own types rather than a disguised oversized refund. The laboratory has no disk persistence or distributed consumption. The lock demonstrates exclusion within one local authority; a real service needs an equivalent transaction or conditional write.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: One shared sum function

blocks.code:
(defn explain-statement [entries]
  (let [sum-kind (fn [kind]
                   (reduce + (map :cents
                     (filter #(= kind (:kind %)) entries))))
        purchases (sum-kind :purchase)
        refunds (sum-kind :refund)
        payments (sum-kind :payment)
        signed (- purchases refunds payments)]
    {:purchases purchases
     :refunds refunds
     :payments payments
     :amount-due (max 0 signed)
     :credit-balance (max 0 (- signed))}))
blocks.caption: Illustrative, unexecuted Clojure; simplified rules equivalent to the laboratory.

blocks.text: The reducer separates purchases, refunds and payments. When the signed balance is negative, it presents a statement credit balance rather than a negative amount due. This preserves financial meaning when the visible payable total is bounded at zero. Both quantities remain reconcilable.

App, PDF and support should consume the same projection or a shared calculation contract with an explicit revision. Copying the formula across three clients increases divergence risk. Real implementation must add accounting-approved categories and cross-channel parity tests. The function does not decide posting dates or whether a merchant actually returned funds.

def test_three_refunds_reduce_exactly_once(self):
        for i, cents in enumerate((3333, 3333, 3334)):

            self.s.append(refund)

Other tests reject missing purchase provenance, excess refund, identity conflict and invalid cents. The concurrency test attempts two 6,000 refunds against 10,000 and accepts only one. Real contractual rules, closing, tax and interest are not tested. These limits should be visible before using the example as an implementation reference.

pages.title: Success means demonstrated understanding

blocks.text: Baselines are unknown. The experiment uses equivalent tasks and comparable groups with the same financial calculation. It measures accuracy and time without confusing a faster screen with better understanding. Screen readers must announce sign, value and linkage; color cannot be the sole signal of credit.

Contact classification is audited so a financial error is not mislabeled as customer confusion. The canary stops for sum divergence, mixed revisions or worse understanding among assistive-technology users. Detail clicks indicate use rather than success. Final validation asks participants to explain the balance in their own words.

pages.title: Economics depend on avoided questions

blocks.text: Annual assumptions: 200,000, 500,000 or 1 million eligible refunds; 0.005, 0.015 or 0.025 fewer interpretive contacts per refund; R$ 16 per contact. Assumed implementation: R$ 120,000; operations: R$ 24,000/year. The calculation values support capacity, not credit returned to the customer.

In the base case, 500,000 × 0.015 × 16 = R$ 120,000. After operations and implementation, year one is −R$ 24,000. Break-even requires 600,000 refunds equivalent to the base assumption. If the product already has a common projection, incremental investment may be lower; the estimate must be redone without automatically carrying over the assumed benefit.

blocks.title: Do not count the same journey twice
blocks.text: Exclude duplication contacts covered in case 10 and allocation contacts in 09. Released hours become cash only through concrete spending changes. This study has observed no Nubank incidence rate or saving.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: A calculation-and-language roadmap

blocks.text: The 90-day period is a planning assumption. Representative examples of partial refunds, payments and closing are needed first, using authorized access or synthetic data. Without that coverage, an attractive screen may work only for the simple case and fail on the journey that generates contact.

Staff defines revision and invariants; accounting approves semantics; design validates language; the EM protects research and iteration capacity. Acceptance is not a checklist of rendered components. Customers must recognize credit origin and understand balance, while support reproduces the explanation using the same reference.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: Operations with an identifiable fallback

blocks.text: The projection first runs in shadow and compares sums with the financial reference. During the canary, calculation detail appears on demand for a limited cohort. If revision changes during lookup, the interface announces the update and recomputes the complete set rather than replacing only the total while retaining old details.

Alerts cover orphan credits, excess principal refunds and cross-channel revision divergence. The projection team investigates processing; accounting resolves semantics; support distinguishes questions from errors. Logs carry references rather than complete purchase descriptions or personal documents.

Rollback hides the new breakdown and retains the canonical balance, preserving IDs for investigation. An exercise should simulate repeated events, refund arrival before purchase and an older PDF revision. Reconciliation must explain why an event was rejected or awaited a dependency. A credit must never be silently discarded because it arrived out of order.

pages.chapter_title: A refund in three entries: the statement must explain its own sum

pages.title: My contribution to trust in the sum

blocks.text: As Staff, I would define a financial representation preserving sign, origin and revision. I would avoid three independent calculations for app, PDF and support. The technical choice is an explainable projection with a canonical source and explicit out-of-order policy, without making the interface a financial authority.

As Engineering Manager, I would organize delivery with accounting, experience, accessibility and operations. I would reserve time to observe users interpreting difficult scenarios, because understanding does not automatically emerge from a correct table. The backlog would cover language and support as well as processing and telemetry.

I would reject solving the issue solely by changing refund color or adding an applied badge. That strengthens a claim without making it verifiable. The tradeoff is enough detail without overwhelming the initial screen: a simple summary, progressive explanation and a total rigorously linked to revision. These are proposed contributions, not claims of previous work at the bank.

The solution does not depend on hiding history or teaching customers to manually redo every accounting calculation. The laboratory demonstrates a small contract that product and accounting can discuss.

Proceed only if the projection reconciles, language improves understanding and assistive guardrails hold. Financial error requires ledger correction first. If the issue is interpretive, an experiment can validate a smaller improvement. The case is stronger when it respects that distinction, including the fact that the historical complaint was resolved.

blocks.text: The customer mentions home video, but no public URL was verified in the captures. The book uses the real page as documentary evidence; it invents no recording, signature or delivery photo.

pages.chapter_title: Delivered in tracking, missing in hand: separate delivery from possession

pages.title: A supplier states a fact; the product decides a state

blocks.text: A carrier event may reliably record what the carrier declared while remaining insufficient to establish possession by the recipient. The journey should preserve that distinction. Declared delivery, disputed delivery and secure activation have different authorities; collapsing them into one status prevents handling disagreement without overwriting information.

The hypothesis is that some repeated reissues can be avoided when events, card issues and shipments have their own identities and an end-to-end exception owner. I would reconstruct authorized journeys by card generation, distinguishing initial loss, replacement order, reissue and late events. If recurrence has another origin, such as address or route performance, the plan must address that demonstrated operational cause.

The study does not conclude that a supplier falsified delivery or that the bank used a particular integration. Investigation should seek proof, provenance, time and escalation policy with minimum access. Customers should not need to publicly expose an address, signature or home video to obtain tracking and support.

pages.chapter_title: Delivered in tracking, missing in hand: separate delivery from possession

pages.title: The old card cannot govern the new one

blocks.title: Shipment, generation and dispute
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The gateway preserves event identity and shipment reference. The record links each shipment to a card generation. Consistency checks route old events and disputes to controlled decisions without silently changing the current card.

The customer disputes receipt through an authenticated channel. Reissue creates a new generation and cancels the earlier card under policy; it is not an automatic consequence of any delay. Secure activation remains a separate contract. The external provider receives neither an internal technology logo nor authority to activate the card.

pages.chapter_title: Delivered in tracking, missing in hand: separate delivery from possession

pages.title: Core: generation and persistent dispute

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_12.py; synthetic local state for one account.

blocks.text: An old-generation event is recorded but cannot alter the current card. Repeated delivery also cannot clear a dispute. The model distinguishes carrier declaration, dispute and activation, preventing a webhook from automatically turning delivery into authorized use.

The supplied scope is trusted context injected by the server, not a freely submitted user credential. Partner signatures and real activation factors are not implemented. A dispute blocks activation in this model; operational resolution needs a separate workflow, while reissue creates another controlled generation.

pages.chapter_title: Delivered in tracking, missing in hand: separate delivery from possession

pages.title: Normalize without losing provenance

blocks.code:
(defn accept-delivery [state event]
  (cond
    (not= (:generation state) (:generation event))
    (assoc state :last-event-result :old-generation)

    (= :delivered (:type event))
    (assoc state :carrier-state :delivered)

    (= :customer-dispute (:type event))
    (assoc state :disputed? true :active? false)

    :else state))
;; Carrier delivery does not clear :disputed? or set :active?.
blocks.caption: Illustrative Clojure, not executed; not carrier or Nubank code.

blocks.text: The reducer does not discover physical truth from a status. It applies precedence and preserves the dispute. Normalization should retain the original event under restricted access alongside the common product state. Otherwise, details needed for investigation disappear during translation across suppliers.

Integration authenticates origin, limits replay and validates shipment/account linkage. An incoming timestamp cannot order the entire card lifecycle: clocks differ and suppliers may resend old information. Generation and identity provide stronger protection against an update for a canceled card appearing to confirm the new one.

    def test_replayed_delivery_cannot_clear_dispute(self):
        self.d.event('d1', 1, 'delivered', 'carrier')
        self.d.event('c1', 1, 'dispute', 'customer')
        self.d.event('d1', 1, 'delivered', 'carrier')
        self.d.event('d2', 1, 'delivered', 'carrier')
        self.assertEqual(self.d.state(), (1, 'delivered', 1, 0))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.d.event('a1', 1, 'activate', 'customer_verified')

blocks.text: The first test shows that old confirmation cannot mark generation two as delivered. The second replays the original webhook and sends another delivery event: the dispute remains open and activation blocked. That property matters more than a happy sequence of messages.

The suite also checks restart, event conflict, incorrect role, stale-generation reissue and cancellation of previous activation. It does not test physical delivery, cryptographic signatures or possession evidence. Integration exercises must validate real suppliers, expiry policies and failures between canceling an old card and issuing a new one.

pages.title: Measure possession and exceptions, not just dispatch

blocks.text: The baseline is unknown. Operational data should connect journey, shipment and generation without exporting addresses to general telemetry. Time to confirmed possession may depend on activation or another approved secure signal; it should not be inferred solely from a carrier event.

The pilot compares equivalent routes and suppliers while controlling seasonality and shipping changes. Fewer reissues count as improvement only if possession or resolution is confirmed. Expansion stops for unauthorized activation, automatic dispute closure or excessive personal-data collection. Cutting cost by refusing necessary replacement is an adverse outcome, not success.

pages.chapter_title: Delivered in tracking, missing in hand: separate delivery from possession

pages.title: Avoided shipping has an economic boundary

blocks.text: Annual assumptions: 50,000, 100,000 or 150,000 eligible shipments; avoided reissues in 0.2%, 0.4% or 0.8% of journeys. That means 100, 400 or 1,200 avoided reissues. I assume R$ 9 per card, R$ 18 shipping and R$ 12 incremental support, totaling R$ 39. No unit cost comes from the complaint.

Assumed implementation: R$ 90,000; operations: R$ 24,000/year. In the base case, 400 × 39 = R$ 15,600; year one is R$ 15,600 − 24,000 − 90,000 = −R$ 98,400. Break-even requires approximately 2,924 avoided reissues in year one. These scenarios do not independently support broad investment; they favor a focused pilot or extension of an existing workflow.

blocks.title: Benefit remains unproven
blocks.text: One customer’s reported count is not a population rate. Do not treat every dispute as fraud or every reissue as avoidable. Support already included in full logistics cost cannot be added again.

pages.title: A roadmap with supplier and operations

blocks.text: The calendar is a 90-day hypothesis. The critical dependency is supplier cooperation, including event quality and evidence access. If that source is unavailable, the first delivery should expose the gap and define an alternative rather than create false certainty in the app.

The EM coordinates logistics, cards, support and partner capacity. Staff defines generation, identity and transitions. Replacement policy needs operational approval and must not emerge as a side effect of a technical retry. Every gate includes a disputed journey, legitimate delivery and a late event for a canceled card.

pages.chapter_title: Delivered in tracking, missing in hand: separate delivery from possession

pages.title: A disputed-delivery runbook

blocks.text: Support opens a case linked to shipment and generation, preserving the customer’s statement. The operator checks provenance and the next authorized action. Reissue without diagnosis is not the only button: investigation, an alternative channel and cancellation of an exposed card require clear policy and ownership.

Alerts separate missing updates, aging disputes and generation-incompatible events. Logistics owns partner follow-up; cards owns cancellation and activation; the service team owns event loss. Sensitive information stays in restricted tools rather than broadly visible tickets.

Rollback disables new interpretation while retaining generation and dispute history. It never reactivates canceled cards. Exercises include a repeated webhook after reissue, delivery assigned to the wrong card and unavailable proof. Reconciliation keeps customers informed without treating a tracking status as conclusive possession evidence.

pages.chapter_title: Delivered in tracking, missing in hand: separate delivery from possession

pages.title: My contribution crosses the physical boundary

blocks.text: As Staff, I would define identity that survives reissue, carrier changes and late events. The central decision is separating declared delivery from secure activation while preserving dispute as its own fact. Architecture must tolerate an imperfect physical world without pretending message ordering resolves delivery truth.

As Engineering Manager, I would establish an owner for the complete exception and an operational forum with the supplier. The team must track resolution and cost per journey, not just cards dispatched. I would reserve capacity for exceptions and align the evidence required to move between stages.

I would reject automatically closing a case when a carrier resends delivered. I would also avoid collecting home videos as a default requirement. The tradeoff is sufficient investigation with minimal data and proportionate cost. Investment should follow verified routes and causes without extrapolating one complaint to the entire operation.

pages.chapter_title: A virtual card cap is not available credit

pages.title: Setting a cap does not grant credit

blocks.text: The product combines at least three concepts: approved credit, remaining global availability and a restriction chosen for a virtual card. A configurable number can look like a purchase promise when wording and hierarchy fail to explain what it controls. This proposal separates those facts and explains the tighter constraint without suggesting that moving a control grants more credit.

The falsifiable hypothesis is that some attempts and contacts result from this confusion rather than an authorization defect. I would observe users explaining what happens when they increase the virtual cap and compare their explanation with subsequent action. I would also investigate freshness: a correct view can become stale when another card consumes shared credit.

Authorization remains independent. Even with available credit, other controls may decline a purchase. The interface should provide current, sufficient information rather than an absolute approval guarantee. The study does not recommend removing risk controls, increasing credit or changing policy to manufacture a better conversion rate.

pages.chapter_title: A virtual card cap is not available credit

pages.title: Credit is shared; reservation is atomic

blocks.title: Local cap and global authority
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The credit source defines the grant; global balance records shared reservations. Card budget adds a restriction while policy and context retain separate controls. The authorizer validates scope and reserves against current authority.

The screen is not a participant in that transaction: its preview can age. The diagram emphasizes authorization, while explainable reads consume versioned projections. Editing a virtual cap never changes global credit. Real risk validation is outside the laboratory and remains necessary for production.

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_13.py; local SQLite reservations with integer cents.

blocks.text: The transaction reads global credit and card budget, checks reservation identity and only then reduces both. Concurrent purchases on different cards cannot spend the same balance. Account-holder authorization precedes return of an idempotent receipt, preventing a key from becoming a way to inspect another person’s operation.

The cap is separate configuration. The laboratory models a synthetic cumulative budget rather than the real product’s period. Reservation expiry, settlement, reversal and risk analysis are not implemented. Preview helps explain, but the financial decision revalidates everything inside the transaction.

blocks.text: Preview takes the smaller of global credit and remaining card budget, bounded at zero. The formula is meaningful only when units, currency and periods are compatible. A real implementation must state those conditions and display its reference time rather than combine a monthly budget with usage from another window.

The component must distinguish chosen cap from available credit in text, without relying on color. Decline messages use safe, actionable reasons without exposing fraud controls. An estimate must not become a guaranteed-approval statement. Server revalidation protects against concurrency; state explanation prevents that protection from appearing arbitrary.

blocks.text: Annual assumptions: 100,000, 250,000 or 500,000 eligible users; 0.004, 0.008 or 0.012 fewer contacts per user; R$ 16 per contact. blocks.text: As Staff, I would separate configuration, projection and authorization. I would define reservation identity, global consistency and read scope. The central technical decision is keeping shared credit in an authority that arbitrates concurrency while experience provides an honest, understandable estimate.

As Engineering Manager, I would align product, credit and risk on terminology and experiment before delivery. The team needs to observe users rather than merely approve screenshots. I would protect accessibility, support and decline-reason analysis time, because improvement depends on language as much as integration.

I would reject relaxing controls to offset poor explanation with a higher approval rate. I would also avoid showing only the minimum number without its origin: that can solve one attempt while leaving confusion intact. The tradeoff is enough information for understanding while preserving risk boundaries and visual simplicity. No proposed contribution assumes my authority over bank policy.

pages.chapter_title: Early repayment received, execution delayed: make the plan verifiable

pages.title: Receiving funds is not executing early repayment

blocks.text: An early-repayment journey involves a discount offer, installment selection, payment and financial application. These events can occur at different times under different rules. The product must distinguish a request, a valid quote, received funds and an obligation actually settled. Without that distinction, a debit can appear to complete an operation still awaiting allocation.

The hypothesis is that a versioned quote linked to the final receipt and exception queue reduces funded operations without understandable execution. I would reconstruct a sample by quote_id and payment_id, comparing rules, validity, receipt and application. I would not assume an interface-only problem: calculation or execution discrepancies belong at the financial authority.

The laboratory proposes a synthetic atomic package of current bill and early repayment. It does not describe Nubank’s current contractual priority. Real rules for partial application, cancellation and discount reversal need validation before implementation. The model supports discussion of the boundary between received money, consent to a plan and an obligation actually settled.

pages.chapter_title: Early repayment received, execution delayed: make the plan verifiable

pages.title: A quote is a contract with expiry

blocks.title: Accepted plan and identifiable execution
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; not Nubank’s internal implementation.

blocks.text: The quote engine uses contract rules and revision to publish an immutable plan. The app queries validity and confirms an identified operation. The financial executor revalidates and applies within its authority, producing its own receipt; lookup does not replace that decision.

Observability signals pending work and discrepancies to the responsible operation, which may pause new offers. The diagram does not authorize a monitor to edit balances. Real settlement, contractual pricing and ledger integration remain necessary; the laboratory reduces them to one account and synthetic amounts.

pages.chapter_title: Early repayment received, execution delayed: make the plan verifiable

pages.title: Core: revalidate before applying

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from labs/case_14.py; transactional execution in cents.

blocks.text: A quote is applied only when revision, validity and received amount agree. Failure before commit rolls back the complete execution. Once completed, a retry returns the original receipt even after expiry; it does not execute another early repayment.

Funds received against an expired or insufficiently funded quote remain recorded for resolution rather than disappearing or silently moving to another price. The laboratory does not implement automatic refunds. Clock and settlement facts must come from trusted server sources, and the supplied discount needs approved contractual calculation.

pages.title: Pure calculation does not replace a transaction

blocks.code:
(defn executable? [quote contract now received]
  (let [required (+ (:bill-cents quote)
                    (- (:principal-cents quote)
                       (:discount-cents quote)))]
    (and (= (:revision quote) (:revision contract))
         (< now (:expires-at quote))
         (>= received required))))

;; Run this check inside the same authority as financial application.
;; The clock, contract and settlement evidence are server-owned.
;; A completed operation returns its original receipt on retry.
blocks.caption: Illustrative, unexecuted Clojure; synthetic rules for contract review.

blocks.text: The function expresses execution conditions, but evaluating it outside the transaction leaves a window for contract change. The service must compare revision and apply the change within the same authority. Required value must include all approved components rather than omit the current bill to make the offer look cheaper.

A material price or plan change requires renewed confirmation. Revalidation does not mean silently recalculating and debiting. History retains the accepted quote, cancellation reason and application receipt. Clojure can keep calculation deterministic; financial integration and event publication remain responsible for atomicity, durability and reconciliation.

def test_received_is_not_executed_and_crash_rolls_back(self):
        self.r.receive('p', 'q', 14000)

The team follows funded-but-unexecuted operations segmented by expiry, insufficiency and stale revision. Every category has an owner and next action; a generic processing status does not replace a resolution plan.

Alerts cover age, amount and discount discrepancy. Credit owns rules; financial platform owns application; operations owns resolution; product owns communication. The runbook forbids applying payment under another plan without authorization. Any refund or compensation remains linked to original funding and quote.

Rollback pauses new offers or the new experience while preserving receipts and received funds. Exercises include crash after commit, expiry during payment, concurrent automatic debit and an old response. Recovery begins with financial authority rather than the screen. Every pending operation must end in valid application or an approved, traceable destination for the money.

pages.chapter_title: Early repayment received, execution delayed: make the plan verifiable

pages.title: My contribution: make the promise executable

blocks.text: As Staff, I would define what accepting a quote means and which authority guarantees execution. I would separate pure calculation, consent, funding and application, with identity and revision at every boundary. I would reject a fix that only changes visual status while the financial operation remains unexecuted.

As Engineering Manager, I would coordinate the teams sharing this journey and expose dependencies in the plan. Support needs the accepted plan and exception reason; accounting needs reconcilable entries; mobile needs stable explanatory semantics. Delivery finishes only when all three work together.

The central tradeoff is offer validity versus friction. Keeping a quote indefinitely can undermine financial rules; unexplained expiry can frustrate customers. I would choose transparent revalidation with renewed consent for material changes. Cost and opportunity would be reassessed in the pilot without claiming gains or authority I do not possess.

pages.title: The incident and its outcome

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: On April 28, 2026, complaint 247218209 described missing Money Boxes and unavailable withdrawals, without a useful support estimate. In its April 30 response, Nubank acknowledged a temporary disruption affecting some customers, stated that assets remained protected, and reported a successful withdrawal from the account on April 28 at 20:46:01. The public status is Answered, with no final customer evaluation. No amount, verified individual duration or evidence of lost assets is disclosed.

The engineering question is how to preserve trustworthy guidance while a dependency is degraded. Olhar Digital reproduced an incomplete screen during this episode and reported recovery; that does not identify an internal cause or quantify affected customers. The following design is my proposal, not a reconstruction of the incident.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: Reading a balance does not authorize withdrawal

blocks.text: I would separate three questions often compressed into one screen: does the investment exist, which position was last verified, and can a withdrawal execute now? A failed query does not answer the other two negatively. Displaying zero because a position did not load confuses availability with ownership; allowing withdrawal against stale information creates another risk. The degraded state must explain the distinction without exposing internal details.

My falsifiable hypothesis is that an auxiliary read could still provide a dated position when withdrawal authority is unavailable. I would inspect existing contracts, shared dependencies, latency budgets and correlated failure history. If reads and writes share an unavoidable outage, an isolated cache may help guidance but cannot restore liquidity. That distinction determines the investment and belongs in the product review.

Investigation would start with synthetic attempts and authorized traces: query started, result unknown, command accepted and receipt confirmed. I would not request customer statements to reproduce the problem. The journey ends when the person receives financial confirmation or an honest explanation of unavailability, with a tracking path and a next update.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: The receipt closes the loop

blocks.title: Dated read; confirmed write
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; technologies illustrate choices, not confirmed internal systems.

blocks.text: Only the financial authority may commit a debit. The journal must persist the result and command identity in one transaction. The proposed outbox publishes already confirmed facts; if transport stops, the customer queries the receipt through an authorized path. Observability receives reduced signals, without amounts or account identifiers in labels.

The dated interface position remains advisory and never crosses this boundary as authorization. The lab represents only local commitment and receipt replay. Custody, settlement, partial outages and service-to-service authorization still require their own contracts and distributed tests.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: One attempt, one commitment

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from the executed lab; imports and initialization are in the full file.

blocks.text: The operation requires a matching owner, positive integer amount and a recent snapshot of the same version. The 30-second clock is an educational assumption, not a Nubank deadline. The advisory balance does not replace authority: with the ledger unavailable, no debit occurs. After success, replaying the same key retrieves the receipt even if the snapshot expired; this prevents a lost response becoming a second withdrawal.

The lock covers one process. In production I would replace this section with a conditional transaction in the durable authority, preserving the same observable semantics. The app does not manufacture trusted snapshots; the test object represents a service-issued read. A receipt also requires access control before deduplication.

pages.title: Dart for an understandable state

blocks.caption: Illustrative Dart example, unexecuted; demonstration copy requires localization.

blocks.text: The interface may offer another authorization attempt without claiming that withdrawal is available. I would present verified amount, timestamp and unavailability as separate facts; screen readers would receive the same distinction. Confirmed state comes from a receipt, not a completed animation. Text and color should reinforce meaning, never carry the explanation alone.

The proposed Clojure service owns the decision while Flutter presents the contract. I would assess existing components before introducing any technology. Deployment starts with unknown state and a queryable receipt, because a new screen without a consistent financial contract merely moves confusion elsewhere in the journey.

blocks.text: UNKNOWN is neither rejection nor confirmation. A consumer can query the same identifier without creating a new financial intent. A changed amount requires a new key; reusing the previous one must fail explicitly. I would define receipt retention against existing obligations and use a much shorter cache lifetime, avoiding deletion of durable evidence when a projection expires.

The owner is resolved from authenticated identity, not supplied as authority in JSON. Logs retain an opaque reference, error class and version. Reconciliation compares committed commands and published events, with restricted permission to investigate discrepancies and without copying balances into operational dashboards.

pages.title: Failures that must not become debits

blocks.caption: Literal test excerpt; all 13 lab tests passed locally.

blocks.text: All thirteen tests passed locally. Beyond these excerpts, the suite covers a wrong owner, conflicting key, future timestamp, exact validity boundary, insufficient funds and invalid monetary types. The race uses two intents against one version; only one may commit funds. The replay test distinguishes an already completed operation from a new request during unavailability.

In the integrated environment I would add a crash after commit but before response, a delayed outbox and replica recovery. The criterion would be one financial movement and a recoverable receipt. This suite measures neither availability, network latency nor custody capacity, and a green run does not authorize real money.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: Metrics that include unknown state

blocks.text: The business baseline is unknown. I would measure confirmed completion: receipts within 60 seconds divided by valid intents, daily, segmented by app version and product. The 60-second window is proposed for discussion, not a published SLA. An intent without a receipt remains unknown until reconciliation and is reported separately, preventing it from disappearing from the denominator.

The second metric is useful guidance: degraded attempts showing a dated position and next step divided by degraded attempts, hourly. The third is repeat contact within 24 hours per affected intent, using pseudonymous linkage and limited retention. The fourth is receipt conflict per committed command; any confirmed financial discrepancy stops the pilot. Sampled traces explain failures without high-cardinality labels.

The experiment compares equivalent journeys under simulated failures, then a small cohort, without deliberately causing financial unavailability. The initial proposed target is reduced contact without increasing unknown outcomes or delaying confirmation. If messaging reduces contact through abandonment or prevents assisted access, the result does not count as success.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: Value without treating balances as revenue

blocks.text: The public case does not disclose an amount. The proposed financial evaluation considers support capacity, not Money Box assets. Exclusively for planning, I assume 20,000 affected intents per month, eight minutes per avoided contact, BRL 60 per loaded hour, BRL 5,000 monthly operating cost and BRL 120,000 implementation cost. None of these inputs is Nubank data.

Monthly formula: intents × absolute contact reduction × minutes ÷ 60 × hourly cost, less operations. Operating break-even requires a 3.125-percentage-point reduction, equivalent to 625 avoided contacts. Recovering implementation would require 40 months in the base scenario and 10.91 in the ambitious scenario, only if freed capacity converts fully into cash; the conservative scenario has no payback under these assumptions.

Finance would need to validate marginal cost, seasonality and how freed hours are used. Redeployed capacity may improve support without reducing expense. I would not add this benefit to other support cases without eliminating overlapping contacts, nor estimate asset loss or recovered revenue from the complaint.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: A 90-day plan with verifiable exits

blocks.text: Days 0–15: the Investments Staff owner maps withdrawal authority with Custody and SRE; Product defines messages for stale positions and unknown outcomes. The deliverable is a contract with failure examples and data classification. Exit requires agreement on who may declare completion, including external dependencies and states without a trustworthy estimate.

Days 16–30: backend implements idempotent lookup and a journal in a test environment while Mobile validates assisted reading and safe retries. QA injects response loss after commitment. Days 31–60: SRE runs state shadowing and reconciliation; expansion requires no discrepancy in the known dataset, complete telemetry and reviewed support documentation.

Days 61–90: the Engineering Manager coordinates a journey-level pilot, cost review and training. Investments accepts integrity; Product accepts comprehension; SRE accepts recovery. Ninety days is a proposed horizon, conditional on existing contracts. Lack of reliable transactional authority blocks pilot writes even if the visual experience is ready.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: Operating when a dependency fails

blocks.text: I would start in shadow mode, calculating the state that would be shown without changing financial authorization. The first cohort receives only queries and explanations; writes progress once receipt recovery has been exercised. A kill switch may remove the new presentation, but must never erase committed operations or turn receipts into generic errors.

The Investments on-call handles differences between journal and position; SRE handles availability and publication lag; Support receives a readable state and the agreed next update. One drill stops the projection while keeping authority available; another stops authority while preserving reads. Both must preserve the distinction between a known position and the current ability to withdraw.

I would stop expansion for an incompatible receipt, another owner’s position, or unknown attempts rising beyond a limit agreed after baseline measurement. Reconciliation gives each pending operation an owner and deadline. A service-restored announcement would not substitute for individual confirmation that a command completed.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: My contribution: trust under failure

blocks.text: As Staff, I would document authority, freshness and idempotency decisions before choosing mechanisms. I would bring the team together to compare three alternatives: a global incident message alone, an advisory cache with receipts, and a withdrawal queue for later execution. My initial preference would be the second because it improves guidance while keeping authorization close to current state. A queue changes timing expectations and requires specific consent; it would not enter scope silently.

As Engineering Manager, I would negotiate capacity across Mobile, Investments, SRE and Support, preventing each team from shipping a different state. Weekly review would examine unknown operations, blocked dependencies and test learning, with documented decisions and explicit owners. The contribution I propose is reduced ambiguity between teams, not perfect availability.

I would present a reproducible test, a known limitation and an economic hypothesis to the review group one at a time. This proposal demonstrates my decision and coordination method; it does not claim involvement in the incident or privileged knowledge of Nubank architecture.

pages.chapter_title: Money Boxes: visible money, reliable withdrawal

pages.title: Handoff: from lab to decision

blocks.text: Run python3 labs/case_15.py -v. Start at Withdrawals.withdraw and follow snapshot, receipts and the ownership check. Change the service from available to unavailable and observe that the balance does not change; then replay a completed operation with the clock advanced and verify that the receipt remains identical. These steps make the key boundary auditable within minutes.

The acceptance checklist includes: no debit without current authority; no duplicate execution on retry; no cross-owner receipt lookup; clearly dated stale positions; trackable unknown outcomes; and reconciliation of delayed publication. Integration still requires real authentication, transactional persistence, custody and settlement policies, trusted clocks, migration and disaster tests.

I would recommend moving only to an integrated prototype if the authority owner accepts this contract and failure tests are reproducible. If a dated query leads people to believe withdrawal is guaranteed, communication design returns to research. Delivery quality includes knowing when to stop an apparent improvement that creates an incorrect financial interpretation.

pages.title: A contradictory answer, a calendar

blocks.caption: Actual crop of the public source, captured 23 October 2026. The text below includes the company reply and reported outcome.

blocks.text: Complaint 250210183, dated June 1, 2026: a Nu+ customer said she transferred investments and was told by chat that she was ineligible, without explanation. On June 9, Nubank confirmed the Treasury investment transfer and eligibility, explaining ten installments starting in June. Status: Answered, with no public confirmation of the first credit. The complaint precedes the first scheduled due date, June 10, so it does not establish overdue cashback.

The consulted rules define a window, net amount and maintenance conditions. The opportunity is to give the customer and Support the same time-aware, versioned explanation. We do not know the individual transferred amount or the original record consulted by the agent; this proposal does not attribute the disagreement to a particular engine.

pages.chapter_title: Portability: eligible does not mean overdue

pages.title: Three questions before declaring an error

blocks.text: I would distinguish eligibility, due date and completed payment. Someone can be eligible in June, have an installment that is not yet due and have no posted credit. If these states become one flag, Support may interpret absent credit as exclusion from the campaign. The hypothesis to test is inconsistent meaning across channels, without assuming that the financial calculation was wrong.

Investigation would follow a synthetic example from custody completion to benefit. It would establish which date counts for the campaign, how outflows offset inflows and which rule revision was accepted. A transfer requested within the window but completed later may need a different answer; the system should show the event used and a review path without exposing third-party holdings.

I would interview Investment Operations and Support about exceptions before modeling automation. The aim is not to turn every complaint into a credit, but to provide a challengeable decision with reproducible facts. Channel disagreement should open a review of the same evidence rather than start another conversation without context.

pages.chapter_title: Portability: eligible does not mean overdue

pages.title: An explainable benefit projection

blocks.title: From custody to calendar
blocks.caption: Proposed external architecture; technologies illustrate choices, not confirmed internal systems.

blocks.text: The source supplies custody facts; the decision component applies a campaign revision; the schedule separates due dates from payments. The executor produces credit only with authorization and current conditions. Reconciliation returns discrepancies for plan review without retroactively changing issued receipts. App and Support would query the same projection, omitted here to keep the main flow visible.

Kafka and Datomic are illustrative choices. An existing implementation may fulfill these responsibilities with other components. The lab represents simplified Nu+ rules only, not every asset, exception or actual maintenance criterion.

pages.chapter_title: Portability: eligible does not mean overdue

pages.title: Calendar before the complaint

blocks.caption: Literal excerpt from the executed lab; imports and initialization are in the full file.

blocks.text: The calculation uses integer cents, net settled inflows within the window and ten due dates. The Nu+ example applies BRL 180 per BRL 30,000 block, capped at BRL 1,800, following the consulted rules. The complaint’s individual amount remains unknown. No payment is allowed before its due date or without explicit subscription and maintenance checks.

After the first credit, a change in the calculated total blocks a new installment and requires reconciliation. Replaying the same installment returns its previous receipt without another effect. The model does not implement retroactive corrections or proportional benefit suspension: those policies must be agreed before replacing its conservative block.

pages.chapter_title: Portability: eligible does not mean overdue

pages.title: One explanation shared by channels

blocks.caption: Illustrative Clojure, unexecuted; not Nubank’s rules engine.

blocks.text: The explanation should show the reason and next action, not just a green or red color. Before the due date, the calendar explains absent credit. After the due date, a missing receipt moves into tracking. When eligibility is challenged, the review should receive the events and rule used without asking the person to retell the story.

I would deploy this function in a domain presentation layer consumed by the app and an authorized support console. Financial authority would remain separate. Copy would be localized and tested for not-yet-due, below-minimum and under-review scenarios. The interface must not infer fraud, noncompliance or customer error from incomplete data.

Maintaining investments is a condition separate from subscription. The campaign owner defines the rule and Operations validates custody evidence; engineering ensures reproducible execution.

The rules available today may differ from historical communication. I would archive the applicable revision and its hash with appropriate legal access. This chapter restricts its example to Nu+, avoiding mixed Ultravioleta figures that differ between the response and public material versions.
